The reflected waves combine, and some wavelengths reinforce while others cancel depending on film thickness and viewing angle. That is interference. Reflection alone would not explain the colour pattern, and diffraction or polarization are not the primary cause here. So option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If the load at the end of a sonometer wire is immersed in a bucket of water, the original fundamental frequency of the wire could be restored by
options: decrease the length of the wire
increasing the length of the wire
increasing the mass per unit length of the wire
changing the temperature of the wire
questions.explanation: For a sonometer wire, the fundamental frequency is proportional to the square root of tension and inversely proportional to length. When the hanging load is immersed in water, its apparent weight decreases because of upthrust, so the wire tension falls and the note becomes lower. To restore the original frequency with smaller tension, the wire length must be reduced. Increasing length or mass per unit length would lower the frequency further.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A boy on looking into a mirror observed that his face appeared to have grown bigger. The boy must have been looking at a
options: convex mirror with his face at the focus
concave mirror with his face between the focus and the mirror
concave mirror with his face at the focus
convex mirror with his face between the focus and the mirror
questions.explanation: A face appearing bigger means the image is magnified and upright. A convex mirror always gives an erect but diminished image, so it cannot fit. A concave mirror produces a magnified upright virtual image only when the object lies between the pole and the focus. At the focus, the image is effectively at infinity, not a normal enlarged face image. Therefore option 1 is the defensible answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Light of velocity 3 x 108ms-1 is incident on a material of reflective of index n. If the velocity of light is reduced to 2.4 x 108ms-1 in the material, what is n?
questions.explanation: The refractive index of a material is the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to its speed in the material: n = c divided by v. With c = 3.0 times 10 to the 8 m per s and v = 2.4 times 10 to the 8 m per s, the powers of ten cancel and n = 3.0 divided by 2.4 = 1.25. Refractive index has no unit. So option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The electromagnetic waves that are sensitive to temperature changes are
questions.explanation: Temperature changes are most directly associated with changes in thermal radiation, and the dominant electromagnetic radiation emitted by ordinary warm bodies is in the infrared region. Infrared detectors are therefore used in heat sensing and thermal imaging. X rays, gamma rays, and ultraviolet are not the relevant part of the spectrum for ordinary temperature variation in this context. Hence option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Three electric cells each of e.m.f 1.5V and internal resistance of 1.0\(\Omega\) are connected in parallel across an external resistance of \(\frac{2}{3}\)\(\Omega\). Calculate the value of the current in the resistor
questions.explanation: Three identical cells in parallel have the same emf as one cell, 1.5 V, but their internal resistances combine in parallel to give 1.0 divided by 3 ohm. The external resistance is 2 over 3 ohm, so total resistance is 2 over 3 plus 1 over 3 = 1 ohm. Current from the battery and through the resistor is 1.5 divided by 1 = 1.5 A. Thus option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A galvanometer of internal resistance 50\(\Omega\) has a full scale deflection for a current of 5mA. What is the resistance required to covert it to a voltmeter with full scale deflection of 10V?
questions.explanation: To make a voltmeter from a galvanometer, a high resistance is added in series so full-scale current still equals the galvanometer current. At full scale, 10 V = 0.005 A times total resistance. Thus total resistance required is 10 divided by 0.005 = 2000 ohm. Since the galvanometer already has 50 ohm, the extra series resistance must be 2000 minus 50 = 1950 ohm. Option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If 8 x 10\(^{-2}\) J of work is required to move 100\(\mu\)C of charge from a point X to a point Y in an electrical circuit, the potential difference between X and Y is
questions.explanation: Potential difference is work done per unit charge: V = W divided by Q. Here W = 8 times 10 to the minus 2 J and Q = 100 microcoulomb = 100 times 10 to the minus 6 C = 1 times 10 to the minus 4 C. Therefore V = 8 times 10 to the minus 2 divided by 1 times 10 to the minus 4 = 8 times 10 squared V = 800 V. Option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In a meter bridge experiment, two resistor 2\(\Omega\) and 3\(\Omega\) occupy the left and right gaps respectively. Find the balance point from the left side of the bridge
questions.explanation: For a meter bridge at balance, the ratio of the left and right gap resistances equals the ratio of the corresponding wire lengths: 2 over 3 = L over 100 minus L. Solving gives 2 times 100 minus L = 3L, so 200 minus 2L = 3L, hence 5L = 200 and L = 40 cm. Since the question asks from the left end, option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Two 50\(\mu\)F parallel plate capacitors are connected in series. The combined capacitor is then connected across a 100-V battery. The charge on each plate of the capacitor is
questions.explanation: Two equal capacitors in series have equivalent capacitance Ceq = C divided by 2, so Ceq = 25 microfarad. Connected across 100 V, the charge in the series combination is Q = Ceq V = 25 times 10 to the minus 6 times 100 = 2.5 times 10 to the minus 3 C. In series, each capacitor carries the same magnitude of charge. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: What is the total electrical energy consumed by using an electric cooker rated 1000W for 5 hrs?
questions.explanation: Electrical energy consumed is power multiplied by time. The cooker power is 1000 W and 5 hours equals 5 times 3600 = 18000 s. Therefore energy = 1000 times 18000 = 1.8 times 10 to the 7 J. Watt times second gives joule, so the unit is correct. This matches option 2. No hidden conversion issue appears in the arithmetic.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The power dissipated in an a.c. circuit with an r.m.s, current of 5A, r.m.s voltage of 10V and a phase angle of 60o is
questions.explanation: Real power in an alternating-current circuit is P = Vrms Irms cos phi. With Vrms = 10 V, Irms = 5 A, and phase angle 60 degrees, P = 10 times 5 times cos 60 degrees = 50 times 0.5 = 25 W. The 50 VA value would be apparent power, not actual power dissipated. Therefore the correct option is 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The voltage of the domestic electric supply is represented by the equation V = 311 sin314.2t. Determine the frequency of the a.c. supply [\(\pi\) = 3.142]
questions.explanation: A sinusoidal supply has the form V = Vmax sin omega t. From V = 311 sin 314.2t, the angular frequency is omega = 314.2 rad per second. Using omega = 2 pi f, the frequency is f = 314.2 divided by 2 times 3.142 = 50.0 Hz. The 311 is the peak voltage, not the frequency. So option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In a purely inductive circuit, the current
options: lags behind the voltage in phase by 90o
leads the voltage in phase by 90o
is in the same phase with the voltage
questions.explanation: In a pure inductor, induced emf opposes the change in current, making the voltage reach its peak before the current does. The phase difference is 90 degrees, with voltage leading current, or equivalently current lagging voltage by 90 degrees. The current is therefore neither in phase nor leading. Hence option 0 states the correct relationship for a purely inductive circuit.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: One of the features of the fission process is that
options: the sum of the masses of the reactants equals the sum of masses of the products
questions.explanation: A heavy nucleus undergoing fission splits into lighter nuclei and releases extra neutrons. Those neutrons can strike other fissile nuclei and trigger further fissions, producing a chain reaction if conditions allow. The products are usually radioactive, neutrons are released, and some mass is converted into energy, so reactant and product masses are not equal. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is the dimension of pressure?
questions.explanation: Pressure equals force divided by area. The dimension of force is mass times acceleration, so force has dimension MLT to the minus 2. Dividing by area, which has dimension L squared, gives pressure dimension MLT to the minus 2 divided by L squared = ML to the minus 1 T to the minus 2. That matches option 0 exactly. The negative power of length is essential.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The length of a displaced pendulum ball which passes its lowest point twice every seconds is [g = 10ms-2]
questions.explanation: The pendulum passes its lowest point twice in one full oscillation. If it does this twice every second, then one complete oscillation takes 1 s, so T = 1 s. For a simple pendulum, T = 2 pi square root of L over g. Hence L = gT squared divided by 4 pi squared = 10 divided by about 39.5, giving roughly 0.25 m. Option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When a ball rolls on a smooth level ground, the motion of its center is
questions.explanation: A rolling ball has both translational motion of its centre of mass and rotational motion about that centre. Since the question asks specifically about the motion of the centre, the relevant description is translational motion along the ground. Oscillatory and random are clearly inapplicable, and rotational describes the body, not the path of its centre. Therefore option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A body is projected from the earth's surface with the intention of letting it escape from the earth's gravitational field. What is the minimum escape velocity of the body? [Earth's radius = 6.4 x 103km, g = 10ms-2]
questions.explanation: Escape velocity from the Earth’s surface is v = square root of 2gR. Using g = 10 m per s squared and Earth’s radius 6.4 times 10 to the 3 km = 6.4 times 10 to the 6 m, we get v = square root of 2 times 10 times 6.4 times 10 to the 6 = square root of 1.28 times 10 to the 8, about 1.13 times 10 to the 4 m per s. That is 11.3 km per s, so option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A uniform rod PQ of length 1m and mass 2kg is pivoted at the end p. If load of 14N is placed at the center of the rod, find the force that should be applied vertically upwards at Q to maintain the rod at equilibrium horizontally [g = 10ms-2]
questions.explanation: Take moments about the pivot at P. The rod’s weight is 2 times 10 = 20 N acting at its centre, 0.5 m from P. The added 14 N load is also at the centre. Total clockwise moment is 20 plus 14, all times 0.5, giving 17 N m. If an upward force F acts at Q, 1 m from P, equilibrium requires F times 1 = 17. Hence F = 17 N. Option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A vehicle of mass m is driven by an engine of power P from rest. Find the minimum time it will take to acquire a speed
questions.explanation: To minimize the time, the engine must deliver its full constant power throughout the acceleration. Power is the rate of doing work, so Pt equals the gain in kinetic energy from rest, which is one-half mv squared. Rearranging gives t = mv squared divided by 2P. The dimensions reduce to seconds, confirming consistency. Therefore option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The energy contained in a wire when it extended by 0.02m by a force 500 N is
questions.explanation: The elastic energy stored when a wire is stretched from zero force to a final force F is one-half F times extension, because the force rises from zero to F during the stretch. Using F = 500 N and extension = 0.02 m, energy = 0.5 times 500 times 0.02 = 5 J. The unit is joule. Therefore the correct choice is option 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A hydraulic press has a large circular piston of radius 0.8m and a circular plunger of radius 0.2m. A force of 500N is exerted by the plunger. Find the force exerted on the piston
questions.explanation: In a hydraulic press, pressure is transmitted equally, so force divided by area is the same on the plunger and piston. Since area is proportional to radius squared, the output force is 500 times 0.8 squared divided by 0.2 squared. This is 500 times 0.64 divided by 0.04 = 500 times 16 = 8000 N. Therefore option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The volume of an air bubble increases from the bottom to the top of a lake at constant temperature because
options: atmospheric pressure acts on the surface of the lake
questions.explanation: At constant temperature, Boyle’s law applies to the air bubble: pressure times volume is constant. Liquid pressure is greater at greater depth, so the bubble is more compressed at the bottom of the lake. As it rises, the surrounding pressure decreases and its volume increases. Upthrust affects the bubble’s motion, not the direct reason for the expansion. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Temperature is the measure of the
options: quantity of heat transferred into the molecules of an object
mean kinetic energy of the molecules of the object
kinetic energy of any individual molecule of the substance
amount of work done by the molecules of the object
questions.explanation: In kinetic theory, temperature measures the average kinetic energy of the random motion of the molecules of a substance. It is not the total heat put into the object, not the kinetic energy of one particular molecule, and not the work done by the molecules. The word mean or average is the key distinction. Therefore option 1 gives the correct physical interpretation.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A rectangular metal block of volume 10\(^{-6}\)m\(^3\) at 273k is heated to 573k. If its coefficient of linear expansion is 1.2 x 10\(^{-5}\)k\(^{-1}\), the percentage change of it volume is
questions.explanation: For an isotropic solid, the coefficient of volume expansion is about three times the linear coefficient. Thus beta = 3 times 1.2 times 10 to the minus 5 = 3.6 times 10 to the minus 5 per kelvin. The temperature rise is 573 minus 273 = 300 K. So fractional volume increase is beta delta T = 3.6 times 10 to the minus 5 times 300 = 0.0108, which is 1.08 percent, about 1.1 percent. Option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A piece of wood floats inside water at room temperature with a fraction of it above the liquid surface. As the temperature of the water is raised, the part of the wood above the liquid will
options: decrease because the density of water decreases with temperature
increase because the density of water decreases with temperature
decreases because the density of water increases with water temperature
increase because the density of water increases with temperature
questions.explanation: A floating object displaces water whose weight equals the object’s weight. As water temperature rises, its density generally decreases, so a larger volume of water must be displaced to provide the same upthrust. That means more of the wood becomes submerged and the fraction above the surface gets smaller. Therefore the part above the liquid decreases because the density of water decreases with temperature. Option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The equation PxVyTz = constant in charles' law when
questions.explanation: Charles’ law states that for a fixed mass of gas at constant pressure, volume is directly proportional to absolute temperature. Therefore V divided by T is constant. In the form P to the x times V to the y times T to the z equals a constant, constant pressure means x = 0, while V over T means y = 1 and z = minus 1. This matches option 1 exactly.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An electric kettle with negligible heat capacity is rated at 2000W. If 2.0kg of water is put in it, how long will it take the temperature of water to rise from 20OC to 100OC? [specific heat capacity of water = 4200Jkg-1k-1]
questions.explanation: The required heat is found from Q = mcΔT because the kettle heat capacity is negligible. With m = 2.0 kg, c = 4200 J kg−1 K−1, and temperature rise ΔT = 100 − 20 = 80 K, Q = 2.0 × 4200 × 80 = 672000 J. Since power P = Q divided by t, t = Q/P = 672000/2000 = 336 s. This corresponds to option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A temperature scale has a lower fixed point of 40mm and a upper fixed point of 200mm. What is the reading on this scale when a thermometer reads 60oC?
questions.explanation: Assuming a linear thermometer scale, 0 degrees Celsius corresponds to 40 mm and 100 degrees Celsius to 200 mm. The 100-degree interval therefore spans 160 mm. At 60 degrees Celsius, the rise above the lower fixed point is 60 percent of 160 mm, which is 96 mm. Adding the lower fixed-point reading gives 40 + 96 = 136 mm. So option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following statements give the TRUE difference between evaporation and boiling? i. Evaporation occurs at all temperatures while boiling occurs at a fixed temperature for a given pressure. ii. Evaporation is a surface phenomenon while boiling is an interior phenomenon. iii. Evaporation is affected by surface area while boiling is not.
questions.explanation: Statement i is true because evaporation can occur at any temperature, whereas boiling occurs at a definite temperature for a given pressure. Statement ii is true because evaporation happens at the surface while boiling occurs throughout the liquid. Statement iii is also accepted as true at this level because evaporation depends strongly on exposed surface area, whereas boiling mainly depends on reaching the boiling condition. Therefore all three statements are correct, so option 3 is right.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A well-lagged bar of length 100cm has its ends maintained at 100oC and 40oC respectively. What is the temperature at a point 60cm from the hotter end?
questions.explanation: In a uniform well-lagged bar at steady state, temperature changes linearly with distance. The temperature drops from 100 degrees Celsius to 40 degrees Celsius over 100 cm, a total drop of 60 degrees. So the gradient is 60 divided by 100 = 0.6 degree per cm. At 60 cm from the hotter end, the drop is 0.6 times 60 = 36 degrees, giving 100 minus 36 = 64 degrees Celsius. Option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is the exclusive property of a transverse wave?
questions.explanation: Polarization is the distinguishing property because it can occur only for transverse waves. In a transverse wave, vibrations are perpendicular to the direction of propagation, allowing restriction to a particular plane. Diffraction and refraction occur for both transverse and longitudinal waves, and compression is characteristic of longitudinal waves. Therefore the exclusive property asked for is polarization, which is option 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The difference between sound waves and light waves is that sound waves
options: are transverse while light waves are longitudinal
require a medium to travel while light waves does not
can be diffracted but light waves cannot
cannot be reflected but light waves can
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave, so it needs a material medium such as air, water, or solids in order to propagate. Light is an electromagnetic wave and can travel through a vacuum. The other alternatives are wrong because sound in air is mainly longitudinal, both sound and light can be reflected, and both can be diffracted under suitable conditions. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The pitch of an acoustic device can be increased by
questions.explanation: Pitch is determined by frequency. A higher frequency means more vibrations per second and is perceived by the ear as a higher pitch. Amplitude and intensity mainly affect loudness, not pitch, and decreasing loudness does not itself raise the note. Therefore the only option that correctly increases pitch is increasing the frequency. That makes option 0 correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Total eclipse of the sun occurs when the
options: earth is between the moon and the sun
sun is between the moon and the earth
moon is between the sun and the earth
questions.explanation: A total eclipse of the Sun occurs when the Moon comes directly between the Sun and the Earth and blocks sunlight from reaching part of the Earth. If the Earth were between the Sun and Moon, that would instead be a lunar eclipse. The ozone layer has nothing to do with eclipse geometry. Therefore option 2 correctly describes the arrangement required for a total solar eclipse.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: What is the approximate critical angle for total internal reflection for diamond if the refractive index of diamond is 2.42?
questions.explanation: For a ray passing from diamond to air, the critical angle C satisfies sin C = n_air divided by n_diamond, which is approximately 1 divided by 2.42 = 0.413. Taking the inverse sine gives C about 24.4 degrees. Among the listed approximations, 24 degrees is the closest. The physically correct interpretation is the onset angle in the denser medium for total internal reflection into air.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following pairs of colours gives the widest separation in the spectrum of white light?
questions.explanation: In dispersion of white light, red and violet are the extreme visible colours. Violet deviates the most because the refractive index is greatest for shorter wavelengths, while red deviates the least. Therefore the separation between red and violet is the widest in the spectrum. Pairs like green and yellow or red and indigo are less widely separated. Hence option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Two parallel plates at a distance of 8.0 x 10-3m apart are maintained at a p.d of 600 volts with the negative plate earthed. What is the electric field strength?
questions.explanation: Between parallel plates, electric field strength is potential difference divided by separation: E = V over d. Using V = 600 V and d = 8.0 times 10 to the minus 3 m, E = 600 divided by 0.008 = 75000 V per m. Earthing the negative plate only fixes its potential reference and does not change the field magnitude set by V and d. Therefore option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: At different locations on the earth's surface, the earth's magnetic field is
options: the same in magnitude and direction
the same in magnitude but different in direction
different in both magnitude and direction
different in magnitude but different in direction
questions.explanation: The Earth’s magnetic field changes from place to place. Both its strength and its direction vary with latitude, longitude, altitude, and local geological conditions. Direction changes are reflected in magnetic declination and dip, while magnitude also varies geographically. Therefore the best statement is that the field is different in both magnitude and direction. Option 2 expresses this clearly; option 3 is just a poorly phrased duplicate.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If a resistance is halved in value and the potential difference across it is tripled, then the ratio of the new current to the old one is
questions.explanation: By Ohm’s law, current equals voltage divided by resistance. Let the original current be I = V over R. If the voltage is tripled and the resistance is halved, the new current becomes 3V divided by R over 2, which equals 6V over R. Therefore the new current is six times the old current. The ratio of new current to old current is 6 to 1, so option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A 12V battery has an internal resistance of 0.5W.If a cable of 1.0W resistance is connected across the two terminals of the battery, the current drawn from the battery is
questions.explanation: Treat the printed W symbols as intended ohms. The battery emf is 12 V, internal resistance is 0.5 ohm, and the connected cable provides 1.0 ohm external resistance. The current drawn from the battery is the complete-circuit current I = E divided by R plus r = 12 divided by 1.5 = 8.0 A. This matches option 1, not 16.0 A.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The purpose of a dielectric material in a parallel plate capacitor is to
options: insulate the plate from each other
increase the magnetic field between the plates
questions.explanation: For a parallel-plate capacitor, capacitance is C = epsilon A divided by d. When a dielectric is inserted, the permittivity becomes k times that of free space, with k greater than 1 for ordinary dielectrics. Hence the capacitance increases. Although a dielectric is an insulator, the main electrical purpose in this context is not merely separating plates but increasing charge storage for the same potential difference.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An electric current of 2 amperes flows in a heating coil of resistance 50 ohms for 3 minutes 20 seconds. Determine the heat produced
questions.explanation: Heat produced in a resistor is given by Joule’s law, H = I squared R t. Here I = 2 A, R = 50 ohms, and time is 3 minutes 20 seconds = 200 s. So H = 2 squared times 50 times 200 = 40000 J = 40.0 kJ. The numerical work, unit conversion, and final option are consistent.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If the maximum voltage across a 100ohms resistor is 20V, then the maximum power it can dissipate is
questions.explanation: For a resistor, the instantaneous power is p = v squared divided by R, so the greatest power occurs when the voltage is at its maximum magnitude. Using Vmax = 20 V and R = 100 ohms gives Pmax = 20 squared over 100 = 400 over 100 = 4.00 W. The physically correct choice is therefore the option reading 4.00 W, at zero-based index 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is required to convert a milliammeter to an ammeter?
questions.explanation: To convert a milliammeter into an ammeter, most of the current must bypass the delicate meter movement. That is done by connecting a shunt of very low resistance in parallel with the meter. A high resistance in series would instead restrict current and is associated with voltmeter conversion. Therefore the required component is a low resistance connected in parallel.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The primary winding of a transformer has 400 turns and its secondary has 100 turns. If a source of e.m.f. of 12V is applied to the primary, the secondary e.m.f. will be
questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer, secondary voltage is proportional to turns ratio: Vs over Vp equals Ns over Np. With Np = 400, Ns = 100, and Vp = 12 V, we get Vs = 12 times 100 divided by 400 = 3 V. Since the secondary has fewer turns, the transformer steps voltage down. Therefore the correct secondary e.m.f. is 3 V.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A light of energy 5eV falls on a metal and the electrons with a maximum kinetic energy of 2eV are ejected. The work function of the metal is
questions.explanation: Einstein’s photoelectric equation states that photon energy equals work function plus maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electron. Hence phi = 5 eV minus 2 eV = 3 eV. No unit conversion is needed because both terms are already in electron-volts. Therefore the metal’s work function is 3.0 eV, matching option 2 exactly.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If it takes 5.0 hrs to drain a container of 540.0m\(^3\) of water, what is the flow rate of water from the container in kgs\(^{-1}\)? [Density of water = 1000kgm\(^{-3}\)]
questions.explanation: The intended flow rate is mass per second, despite the awkward printed unit. First find the mass of water: m = density times volume = 1000 times 540 = 540000 kg. The draining time is 5.0 h = 18000 s. So mass flow rate = 540000 divided by 18000 = 30.0 kg per second. Thus the correct option is 30.0 kg s minus 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A boat travels due east at a speed 40ms\(^{-1}\)s across a river flow due south at 30ms\(^{-1}\)s. What is the resultant speed of the boat?
questions.explanation: The attached sketch shows two perpendicular velocity components: 40 m s minus 1 due east and 30 m s minus 1 due south. The resultant speed is the magnitude of their vector sum, found by Pythagoras: v = square root of 40 squared plus 30 squared = square root of 2500 = 50 m s minus 1. Only the magnitude is asked, so direction is not needed.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An object is projected with a velocity of 80ms-1 at an angle of 30o to the horizontal.The maximum height reached is
questions.explanation: Maximum height of a projectile is H = u squared sin squared theta divided by 2g. With u = 80 m s minus 1, theta = 30 degrees, sin 30 degrees = 0.5, and the usual exam value g = 10 m s minus 2, H = 80 squared times 0.25 divided by 20 = 1600 divided by 20 = 80 m. So the correct answer is 80 m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A motor vehicle is brought to rest from a speed of 15ms-1 in 20 seconds. Calculate the retardation.
questions.explanation: Use uniform acceleration: a = v minus u over t. The vehicle starts at 15 m s minus 1 and comes to rest, so v = 0 and t = 20 s. Hence a = 0 minus 15 over 20 = minus 0.75 m s minus 2. Retardation means the magnitude of this negative acceleration, which is 0.75 m s minus 2. The option’s printed unit is faulty, but its value identifies the answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is TRUE of a particle moving in a horizontal circle with constant angular velocity?
options: The energy is costant but the linear momentum varies
The linear momentum is conatant but the energy varies
both energy and linear momentum are constant
The speed and the linear velocity are both constant
questions.explanation: In horizontal circular motion with constant angular velocity, the speed stays constant, so kinetic energy remains constant because it depends on v squared. Linear momentum, however, is a vector. Its magnitude mv stays the same, but its direction changes continuously around the circle. Therefore momentum is not constant even though energy is. So option 0 is the true statement.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An object of mass 50kg is released from a height of 2m.Find the kinetic energy just before it strikes the ground
questions.explanation: Neglecting air resistance, the loss of gravitational potential energy becomes kinetic energy just before impact. So KE = mgh = 50 times 10 times 2 = 1000 J, using the standard school value g = 10 m s minus 2. The arithmetic is direct and the unit is joule. Therefore the correct answer is 1000 J.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A cone in an unstable equilibrium has its potential energy
questions.explanation: A body in unstable equilibrium is at a position where its potential energy is maximum relative to nearby positions. A slight displacement lowers its potential energy and makes it move further away from the original point. Therefore, when describing the state of the cone in unstable equilibrium, its potential energy is increased, not decreased or unchanged. Hence option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Calculate the magnitude of the force required to just move a 20kg object along a horizontal surface if the coefficient of friction is 0.2. [g = 10ms-2]
questions.explanation: To just start moving the object, the applied force must equal the limiting friction. On a horizontal surface, normal reaction R = mg = 20 times 10 = 200 N. Hence friction F = mu R = 0.2 times 200 = 40 N. This is the minimum force required to move it. Therefore the correct option is 40.0 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Calculate the velocity ratio of a screw jack of pitch 0.3cm if the length of the tommy bar is 21cm
questions.explanation: Velocity ratio of a screw jack equals distance moved by the effort in one turn divided by the pitch. In one complete turn, the effort moves through the circumference of the tommy bar: 2 pi r = 2 pi times 21 = 42 pi cm. Dividing by the pitch 0.3 cm gives 42 pi divided by 0.3 = 140 pi. Thus option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A force of 15N stretches a spring to a total length of 30cm. An additional force of 10N stretches the spring 5cm further. Find the natural length of the spring
questions.explanation: The extra 10 N increases the spring length by 5 cm, so by Hooke’s law the spring constant is 10 divided by 5 = 2 N per cm. A 15 N load therefore produces an extension of 15 divided by 2 = 7.5 cm. Since the total length under 15 N is 30 cm, the natural length is 30 minus 7.5 = 22.5 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of these statements are TRUE of pressure in liquids? i. pressure acts equally in all direction. ii. pressure decreases with depth. iii. pressure at the same level of a liquid is the same. iv pressure is dependent on the cross-sectional area of the barometer tube
questions.explanation: Pressure in a liquid at a point acts equally in all directions, so statement i is true. Hydrostatic pressure increases with depth, not decreases, so ii is false. At the same horizontal level in the same liquid, pressure is equal, so iii is true. Pressure does not depend on the cross-sectional area of the containing tube, so iv is false. Therefore i and iii only are correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The mass of a specific gravity bottle is 15.2g when it is empty. it is 24.8g when filled with kerosene and 27.2g when filled with distilled water. Calculate the relative density of kerosene
questions.explanation: Relative density is the mass of a substance divided by the mass of an equal volume of water. Mass of kerosene in the bottle = 24.8 minus 15.2 = 9.6 g. Mass of water = 27.2 minus 15.2 = 12.0 g. So relative density = 9.6 divided by 12.0 = 0.80. Hence the correct answer is option 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If a solid X floats in liquids P of relative density 2.0 and in liquid Q of relative density 1.5, it can be inferred that the
options: weight of P displaced is greater than that of Q
weight of P displaced is less than that of Q
volume of P displaced is greater than that of Q
volume of P displaced is less than that of Q
questions.explanation: A floating body displaces liquid whose weight equals the body’s own weight. Since the same solid floats in both liquids, the weight displaced is the same in P and Q, so options 0 and 1 are false. Liquid P is denser than Q because its relative density is 2.0 compared with 1.5. To obtain the same upthrust in a denser liquid, a smaller volume is displaced. Therefore option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The melting point of naphthalene is 78oC. What is this temperature in kelvin
questions.explanation: Kelvin temperature is obtained by adding 273 to the Celsius reading. Thus 78 degrees Celsius corresponds to 78 plus 273 = 351 K. This is an offset conversion, not a scaling by any factor. The arithmetic is exact at this level of school convention, so the correct option is 351 K.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A Motor Tyre is inflated to pressure of 2.0 x 105Nm-2 when the temperature of air is 27oC. What will be the pressure in it at 87oC assuming that the volume of the Tyre does not change?
questions.explanation: At constant volume, pressure is directly proportional to absolute temperature, so P1 over T1 equals P2 over T2. Convert temperatures to kelvin: 27 degrees Celsius = 300 K and 87 degrees Celsius = 360 K. Then P2 = 2.0 times 10 to the 5 times 360 over 300 = 2.4 times 10 to the 5 N m minus 2. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When 100g of liquids L1 at 78°C was mixed with Xg of liquid L2 at 50°C, the final temperature was 66°C. Given that the specific heat capacity of L2is half that of L1, find x
questions.explanation: Assuming no heat is lost, heat lost by the hotter liquid equals heat gained by the cooler one. Let the specific heat capacity of L1 be c, so that of L2 is c over 2. Then 100c times 78 minus 66 equals x times c over 2 times 66 minus 50. This gives 100c times 12 = x times 8c, so x = 150 g.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Heat is supplied to a test tube containing 100g of ice at its melting point. The ice melts completely in 1 min.What is the power rating of the source of heat? [Latent heat of fusion of ice = 336Jg-1]
questions.explanation: The source supplies latent heat to melt ice already at its melting point, so Q = mL. With m = 100 g and latent heat L = 336 J per gram, Q = 100 times 336 = 33600 J. Power is energy per time, and 1 minute = 60 s, so P = 33600 divided by 60 = 560 W. Hence option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Two similar kettles containing equal masses of boiling water are placed on a table. If the surface of one is highly polished and the surface of the other is covered with soot, Which of the following observations is correct
options: The two kettles will cool down at the same rate
the polished kettle cools down more quickly by conduction
the kettle covered with soot cools down more quickly because it is a good radiator
the kettle covered with soot cools down more quickly by the process of heat convection
questions.explanation: A dull black or sooty surface is a much better emitter of thermal radiation than a highly polished surface. Since both kettles contain equal masses of boiling water, the key difference in cooling rate comes from radiation from their outer surfaces. The sooty kettle therefore loses heat faster and cools more quickly. Hence option 2 is the correct observation.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The equation of transverse wave traveling along a string is given by Y = 0.3 sin(0.5x - 50t) where Y and X are in cm and t is in seconds.Find the maximum displacement of the particles from the equilibrium position
questions.explanation: A transverse wave written as Y = A sin of a phase term has amplitude A. The amplitude is the maximum displacement of particles from the equilibrium position. Comparing the given equation Y = 0.3 sin(0.5x minus 50t) with the standard form, A = 0.3 cm. Therefore the maximum displacement is 0.3 cm, which is option 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The sound from a source travelled to the bottom of the sea and the echo was heard 4s later. If the speed of sound in sea water is 1500ms-1 the depth of the sea is
questions.explanation: The 4 s stated is the total time for the sound to travel down to the seabed and back as an echo. Therefore the one-way time is 4 divided by 2 = 2 s. Depth = speed times one-way time = 1500 times 2 = 3000 m. Using the full 4 s would incorrectly double the depth. Hence option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The fundamental frequency of vibration of a sonometer wire may be halved by
options: doubling the length of the wire
doubling the mass of the wire
reducing the absolute temperature by half
questions.explanation: For a stretched string, the fundamental frequency is f = 1 over 2L times the square root of T over mu. Keeping tension and linear density unchanged, frequency is inversely proportional to length. Therefore doubling the length makes the frequency half its original value. The other options do not produce an exact halving under the stated relation. So option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A pipe of length 45cm is closed at the end. Calculate the fundamental frequency of the sound wave generated in the pipe if the velocity of sound in air is 360ms-1 [Neglect end correction]
questions.explanation: A pipe closed at one end has fundamental wavelength equal to four times its length, so the fundamental frequency is f = v over 4L. Here v = 360 m s minus 1 and L = 45 cm = 0.45 m. Thus f = 360 divided by 4 times 0.45 = 360 divided by 1.8 = 200 Hz. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The note produced by a stretched string has a fundamental frequency of 400Hz. If the length of the string is doubled while the tension in the string is increased by a factor of 4, the frequency is
questions.explanation: For a stretched string, frequency is proportional to the square root of tension divided by length. Doubling the length multiplies frequency by one-half. Increasing the tension by a factor of 4 multiplies frequency by square root of 4, which is 2. Combined effect is 2 times one-half = 1, so the frequency stays unchanged. It therefore remains 400 Hz.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: To produce a parallel beam of light from a concave mirror, the distance at a which the lamp should be placed from the mirror is equal to
options: two times the radius of curvature
questions.explanation: A concave mirror sends out parallel reflected rays when the light source is placed at its principal focus. This is the standard reverse of the rule that parallel rays incident on a concave mirror meet at the focus after reflection. Therefore the lamp must be placed one focal length from the mirror. Hence option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Light of frequency 6.0 x 10\(^{14}\) Hz travelling in air is transmitted through glass or refractive index 1.5. Calculate the frequency of the light in the glass
questions.explanation: When light passes from air into glass, its speed decreases and its wavelength changes accordingly, but its frequency does not change at the boundary. Frequency is fixed by the source and must remain continuous across media. Therefore the refractive index affects speed, not frequency. The frequency in the glass is still 6.0 times 10 to the 14 Hz, so option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An object is placed in front of a converging lens of a focal length 20cm. The image is virtual and has a magnification of 2. What is the distance of the object from the lens?
questions.explanation: For a converging lens producing a virtual upright image, the magnification is positive and greater than 1, so m = v over u = 2 in magnitude, with image and object on the same side. Using Cartesian signs gives v = minus 2u and f = plus 20 cm. Then 1 over f = 1 over v minus 1 over u gives 1 over 20 = minus 1 over 2u plus 1 over u = 1 over 2u, hence u = 10 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In a projection lantern of focal length f, the object distance u, is such that
questions.explanation: A projection lantern uses a converging lens to form a real enlarged image on a screen. For a convex lens, a real magnified image is produced when the object lies between one focal length and two focal lengths from the lens. If it were beyond 2f, the image would be diminished; at f there would be no screen image. Therefore f less than u less than 2f is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following has the lowest internal resistance when new?
questions.explanation: An accumulator, such as a lead-acid storage battery, is designed to supply comparatively large currents. That requires low internal resistance, especially when new and in good condition. Primary cells like the Leclanche or Daniell cell, and ordinary torch batteries, generally have higher internal resistance. Therefore the option with the lowest internal resistance is the accumulator.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When a biro pen rubbed on a dry silk cloth is moved very close to a piece of paper on a dry table, the pen is found to pick up the paper. This is because
options: both the pen and the cloth are magnetized
the pen is magnetized but the cloth is not
the pen is charged while the cloth is magnetized
both the pen and the cloth are charged
questions.explanation: Rubbing the biro on dry silk produces charging by friction, not magnetization. During rubbing, electrons are transferred so that the pen and the cloth become oppositely charged. The charged pen can then attract nearby bits of paper by electrostatic induction, even if the paper was initially neutral. Therefore the correct statement is that both the pen and the cloth are charged.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A capacitor 8\(\mu\)F is charged to a potential difference of 100V. The energy stored by the capacitor is
questions.explanation: Energy stored in a capacitor is E = one-half C V squared. Here C = 8 microfarads = 8 times 10 to the minus 6 farad and V = 100 V. Thus E = one-half times 8 times 10 to the minus 6 times 100 squared = 4 times 10 to the minus 2 J. The micro prefix is essential. Hence option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Two capacitors R1 = 4\(\Omega\) and R2 = 5\(\Omega\) are connected in parallel across a potential difference. If P1 and P2 represent power dissipated in R 1 and R2 respectively, then the ratio P1 : P2 is
questions.explanation: These are clearly resistors, despite the question mistakenly saying capacitors. In parallel, each resistor has the same potential difference across it. Since power P = V squared over R, the ratio is P1 to P2 = V squared over 4 to V squared over 5 = 1 over 4 to 1 over 5 = 5 to 4. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following are found in the receiver but not in the microphone of a telephone handset? i. Diaphragm. ii. soft iron pole pieces. iii. permanent magnet. iv.carbon blocks
questions.explanation: A telephone receiver contains magnetic parts used to convert current variations into vibrations: a permanent magnet and soft iron pole pieces, along with a diaphragm. A carbon microphone also has a diaphragm, but its distinctive element is carbon granules or blocks rather than the receiver’s magnetic assembly. Therefore the parts present in the receiver but not in the microphone are ii and iii only.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If two parallel conductors carry currents flowing in the same direction, the conducts will
options: both move in the same direction
have no effect on each other
questions.explanation: Each current-carrying conductor produces a magnetic field that acts on the other conductor. For parallel wires carrying current in the same direction, the magnetic interaction is attractive. If the currents were in opposite directions, the force would be repulsive instead. Since the question specifies the same direction, the conductors attract each other. Therefore option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A certain radioisotope of \(^{235}_{92}U\) emits four alpha particles and three beta particles. The mass number and the atomic number of the resulting elements respectively are
questions.explanation: Start with uranium-235, so mass number A = 235 and atomic number Z = 92. Emitting four alpha particles reduces A by 16 and Z by 8, giving A = 219 and Z = 84. Emitting three beta-minus particles leaves A unchanged but increases Z by 3, so Z becomes 87. The resulting numbers are therefore 219 and 87, matching option 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If light with photon energy 2eV is incident suitably on the surface of a metal with work function 3eV, then
options: the few electrons emitted will have a maximum kinetic energy of 1eV
the few electrons emitted will have a maximum kinetic energy of 3eV
questions.explanation: Photoelectric emission occurs only if the photon energy is at least equal to the work function of the metal. Here the incident photon energy is 2 eV while the work function is 3 eV. Since 2 eV is smaller than 3 eV, the photons cannot liberate electrons from the surface. Therefore no electrons will be emitted. Option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following quantities has the same unit as the watt?
questions.explanation: A watt is the unit of power, equal to one joule per second. Force times velocity has units N times m per s, which equals J per s, so it has the same unit as the watt. By contrast, force times distance is work in joules, and force times time is impulse. Therefore the correct quantity is force times velocity.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The external and internal diameter of a tube are measured as (32 ± 2)mm and (21 ± 1)mm respectively. Determine the percentage error in the thickness of the tube.
questions.explanation: Thickness of the tube wall is half the difference of the diameters: t = 32 minus 21 over 2 = 5.5 mm. For subtraction, absolute errors add, so error in the diameter difference is 2 plus 1 = 3 mm. Therefore error in thickness is 3 over 2 = 1.5 mm. Percentage error = 1.5 divided by 5.5 times 100, about 27 percent. Option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Two forces of magnitudes 7N and 3N act at right angles to each other. The angle \(\theta\) between the resultant and the 7N force is given by
questions.explanation: The 7 N and 3 N forces are perpendicular, so together they form the two legs of a right triangle whose hypotenuse is the resultant. If theta is the angle between the resultant and the 7 N force, then the side opposite theta is 3 N and the adjacent side is 7 N. Hence tan theta = 3 over 7. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A rocket burns fuel at the rate of 10kgs-1 and ejects it with velocity of 5 x 103ms-1. The thrust exerted by the gas on the rock is
questions.explanation: Rocket thrust equals the rate of change of momentum of the expelled gas, so F = mass flow rate times exhaust speed. Here the rocket burns fuel at 10 kg per second and ejects it at 5 times 10 to the 3 m per second. Thus F = 10 times 5 times 10 to the 3 = 5.0 times 10 to the 4 N. So option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The force experienced by an object of mass 60.0kg in the moon's gravitational field is 1.002 x 102N. What is the intensity of the gravitational field?
questions.explanation: Gravitational field intensity is force per unit mass, g = F over m. The force is 1.002 times 10 squared N = 100.2 N and the mass is 60.0 kg. Therefore g = 100.2 divided by 60.0 = 1.67 N per kg, approximately. This is reasonable for the Moon because it is much less than Earth’s field strength. Hence option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes the energy changes in the generation of light by a hydroelectric power station?
questions.explanation: Water in a hydroelectric station is stored at height, so its initial energy is gravitational potential energy. When released, that energy drives the turbine, giving mechanical energy, then the generator converts this to electrical energy, and the lamp converts electrical energy to light. Although falling water also has kinetic energy briefly, the best overall sequence among the options begins with potential energy, so option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A plane inclined at angle \(\theta\) has a velocity ratio of 10 : 1. The inclination of the plane to the horizontal is given by
questions.explanation: For an inclined plane, the velocity ratio is distance moved by effort divided by distance moved by load. Geometrically, that is length of plane divided by vertical height, so VR = l/h = 1/sin theta. Given VR = 10, we have 1/sin theta = 10, hence sin theta = 1/10. The selected option matches the geometry and the machine definition exactly.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A weightless vessel of dimensions 4m x 3m x 2m is filled with a liquid of density 1000kgm\(^{-3}\) and sealed. What is the maximum pressure this container can exert on a flat surface? [g = 10ms\(^{-2}\)]
questions.explanation: The vessel is weightless, so the pressure on the surface comes only from the liquid’s weight. Volume = 4 x 3 x 2 = 24 m3. Mass = 1000 x 24 = 24000 kg. Weight = 24000 x 10 = 2.4 x 10^5 N. Maximum pressure occurs when the vessel rests on its smallest face, area 3 x 2 = 6 m2. Hence pressure = 2.4 x 10^5 divided by 6 = 4.0 x 10^4 N m^-2, so option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An object of mass 400g and density 600kgm-3 is suspended with a sting so that half of it is immersed in paraffin of density 900kgm-3. The tension in the string is
questions.explanation: Mass is 0.400 kg, so the weight is about 4 N using g = 10 m/s2. The object volume is m/rho = 0.4/600 = 6.67 x 10^-4 m3, and half immersed means 3.33 x 10^-4 m3 of paraffin is displaced. The upthrust is 900 x 10 x 3.33 x 10^-4 = 3 N. For vertical equilibrium, tension plus upthrust balances weight, so T = 1 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The thermometric properties of the thermocouple is that is
questions.explanation: A thermocouple works by the Seebeck effect. When the junctions of two dissimilar metals are at different temperatures, an electromotive force is produced. That e.m.f. changes with temperature difference and serves as the thermometric property. Resistance change belongs to resistance thermometers, while volume and pressure changes are used in liquid and gas thermometers. Therefore option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A metal rod 800mm long is heated from 10oC to 95oC. If it expands by 1.36mm, the linear expansivity of the metal is
questions.explanation: Use linear expansion: change in length = alpha times original length times temperature rise. Here, change in length is 1.36 mm, original length is 800 mm, and temperature rise is 95 minus 10 = 85 K. So alpha = 1.36 divided by 800 x 85 = 2.0 x 10^-5 K^-1. Using millimetres throughout is valid because the length units cancel. Option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When the volume of a given mass of gas is halved and its temperature doubled, the pressure
questions.explanation: For a fixed mass of gas, pV/T is constant, so pressure is proportional to T/V when temperature is measured on an absolute scale. If the temperature doubles and the volume is halved, the new pressure is proportional to 2T divided by V/2, which equals 4T/V. Therefore the pressure becomes four times the original value. Option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: 200g of water at 90°C is mixed with 100g of water at 30°C. What is the final temperature?
questions.explanation: Since both substances are water, their specific heat capacities are equal and cancel in the heat balance. Heat lost by the hotter water equals heat gained by the cooler water: 200(90 minus T) = 100(T minus 30). Solving gives 18000 minus 200T = 100T minus 3000, so 21000 = 300T and T = 70 degrees Celsius. That corresponds to option 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Determine the distance between the consecutive antinodes XX if the wavelength is 60cm
questions.explanation: In a stationary wave, adjacent nodes are separated by half a wavelength, and adjacent antinodes are also separated by half a wavelength. If the wavelength is 60 cm, the distance between consecutive antinodes is 60/2 = 30 cm. The quarter-wavelength spacing applies between a node and the next antinode, not between two antinodes. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following waves can propagate through a vacuum?
questions.explanation: Sound waves, including ultrasonic and acoustic waves, are mechanical disturbances and require a material medium for propagation. They cannot travel through a vacuum. Infra-red waves are electromagnetic waves, so they do not need a medium and can propagate through empty space. Therefore only infra-red waves satisfy the condition stated in the question. Option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Radio waves emitted from an antenna are picked up by a radar after reflection from an aircraft in 4 x 10\(^{-3}\)S. How far is the aircraft from the antenna? [c = 3 x 10\(^8\)ms\(^{-1}\) ]
questions.explanation: The radar time given is for the journey to the aircraft and back, so the one-way distance is ct/2. Using c = 3 x 10^8 m s^-1 and t = 4 x 10^-3 s gives distance = (3 x 10^8 x 4 x 10^-3)/2 = 6 x 10^5 m. Converting to kilometres gives 6 x 10^2 km, or 600 km. Option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following expressions gives the linear magnification produced by a concave mirror of radius of curvature r, if U and V are the object and image distances respectively?
questions.explanation: For a concave mirror, linear magnification is m = v/u. Also, the mirror formula is 1/f = 1/u + 1/v, with f = r/2. Hence 2/r = 1/u + 1/v, so 1/u = 2/r minus 1/v. Substituting into m = v/u gives m = 2v/r minus 1. Therefore the correct expression is option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If the focal length of a camera lens is 20cm, the distance from the film at which the lens must be set to produce a sharp image of an object 100cm away is
questions.explanation: Use the thin lens formula 1/f = 1/u + 1/v. With focal length 20 cm and object distance 100 cm, 1/v = 1/20 minus 1/100 = 4/100 = 1/25. Therefore v = 25 cm. Since the film must be placed where the real image forms, the lens should be set 25 cm from the film. Option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following may be used to explain a mirage? i. layers of air near the road surface have varying refractive indices in hot weather. ii. road surfaces sometimes become good reflectors in hot weathers. iii. light from the sky can be reflected upwards after coming close to the road surface.
questions.explanation: A mirage is caused by layers of air at different temperatures having different refractive indices, so statement i is correct. Light from the sky bends through these layers and can undergo total internal reflection or strong upward bending near the hot surface, making statement iii acceptable. The road itself does not become a true reflecting surface, so statement ii is false. Thus option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A beam of light is incident from air to water at an angle of 30oC. Find the angle of refraction if the refractive index of water is \(\frac{4}{3}\)
questions.explanation: Apply Snell's law: n1 sin i = n2 sin r. For light going from air to water, n1 = 1, n2 = 4/3, and i = 30 degrees. So sin r = (1 x sin 30 degrees)/(4/3) = (1/2) x (3/4) = 3/8 = 0.375. Therefore r is about 22 degrees. The option values use degree symbols incorrectly as Celsius, but option 2 is numerically correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The property of the eye known as its power of accommodation is controlled by the
questions.explanation: Accommodation is the eye's ability to adjust focal length so that objects at different distances are focused on the retina. This is achieved by changing the curvature of the lens, and that change is controlled by the ciliary muscles. The iris and pupil regulate light intensity, while the vitreous humour mainly helps maintain the eye's shape. Therefore option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following correctly explain(s) why a green leaf appears green in bright day light? i. it absorbs only the green component of sunlight. ii. it absorbs all colour of sunlight except green. iii. it reflects only the green component of sunlight.
questions.explanation: A green leaf appears green because it reflects green light to the eye and absorbs much of the other visible colours. Therefore statement ii is correct and statement iii is also correct. Statement i is false because if the leaf absorbed only green light, it would not appear green. The explanation follows selective absorption and reflection of white sunlight. Option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following correctly explains why soft iron is proffered to steel in electromagnets? i. soft iron is more readily magnetized than steel. ii. soft iron is more readily demagnetized than steel. iii. soft iron retains magnetism more than steel.
questions.explanation: An electromagnet should magnetize strongly when current flows and lose magnetism quickly when the current stops. Soft iron has high permeability, so it is readily magnetized, making statement i true. It also has low retentivity, so it is readily demagnetized, making statement ii true. Statement iii is false because steel retains magnetism better than soft iron. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A current carrying conductor experiences a force when placed in a magnetic field because the
options: magnetic field of the current interacts with external magnetic field
force is due to the motor principle
electric field of the current interacts with the external magnetic field
questions.explanation: A current-carrying conductor produces its own magnetic field. When the conductor is placed in an external magnetic field, the two magnetic fields interact, giving rise to a force on the conductor. That is the physical basis of the motor effect. Simply naming the principle is less explanatory, and electric-field interaction is incorrect here. Therefore option 1 is the correct statement.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A simple cell with mercury-amalgamated zinc electrode prevents
questions.explanation: Amalgamating the zinc with mercury covers impurities on the zinc surface. Those impurities would otherwise form many tiny local cells that corrode the zinc even when the main circuit is open, a process called local action. Polarization is a separate problem caused by gas bubbles at the electrode and is prevented by depolarizers, not by amalgamation. Therefore option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The terminal voltage of a battery is 4.0V when supplying a current of 2.0A, and 2.0V when supplying a current of 3.0A. The internal resistance of the battery is
questions.explanation: For a battery delivering current, terminal voltage is V = E minus Ir. Using the two conditions: 4 = E minus 2r and 2 = E minus 3r. Subtracting the second equation from the first gives 2 = r, so the internal resistance is 2 ohms. Substituting back gives E = 8 V in both cases, confirming consistency. Option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A current of 100mA passes through a conductor for 2 minutes. The quantity of electricity transported is
questions.explanation: Electric charge transported is Q = It. The current is 100 mA = 0.1 A, and the time is 2 minutes = 120 s. Hence Q = 0.1 x 120 = 12 C. The unit is coulomb because 1 ampere times 1 second equals 1 coulomb. Therefore the correct option is 12 C, which is option 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor of area 10cm2 in vacuum has a capacitance of 10-2\(\mu\)F. What is the distance between the plates?(e = 9 x 10-12fm)
questions.explanation: For a parallel-plate capacitor in vacuum, C = epsilon A/d, so d = epsilon A/C. The area is 10 cm^2 = 10 x 10^-4 = 10^-3 m^2, and the capacitance is 10^-2 microfarad = 10^-8 F. Using epsilon = 9 x 10^-12 F m^-1 gives d = (9 x 10^-12 x 10^-3)/(10^-8) = 9 x 10^-7 m. Hence option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A 40-W instrument has a resistance of 90\(\Omega\). On what voltage should it be operated normally?
questions.explanation: Use the relation P = V^2/R for a resistive instrument. Rearranging gives V = square root of PR. Substituting P = 40 W and R = 90 ohms gives V = square root of 3600 = 60 V. This is the operating voltage required for the instrument to dissipate 40 W with that resistance. Therefore option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following devices may be used to step up the voltage in a d.c. circuit?
questions.explanation: A step-up transformer requires alternating current and cannot operate directly on a steady d.c. supply. A wattmeter only measures power, and a d.c. generator is a source rather than a voltage-raising device in an existing circuit. An induction coil uses interrupted direct current and electromagnetic induction to produce a much higher voltage. Therefore option 3 is the correct device.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The primary aim in high tension transmission is to
options: minimize electrical energy losses due to heat production
increase the rate of energy transfer by using high voltage
increase the current in the wire
generate electricity at high current and low voltage
questions.explanation: Electric power transmitted is P = VI. For a given power, raising the transmission voltage reduces the current. Since heat loss in cables is I^2R, a smaller current means much less energy wasted as heat. That is the main purpose of high-tension transmission, not increasing current or generating at low voltage. Therefore option 0 is the correct statement.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Determine the inductive reactance when a 30.0mH inductor with a negligible resistance is connected to a 1.3 x 103Hz oscillator.
questions.explanation: Inductive reactance is X_L = 2 pi fL. Here f = 1.3 x 10^3 Hz and L = 30.0 mH = 3.0 x 10^-2 H. Thus X_L = 2 pi x 1.3 x 10^3 x 3.0 x 10^-2 = 78 pi, which is approximately 245 ohms. Since the resistance is negligible, this is the opposition offered by the inductor. Option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following statements correctly describe(s) cathode rays? i. they consist of tiny particles carrying negative electric charges. ii. they are deflected in a magnetic field but not in an electric field. iii. they consist of fast moving neutrons and deflected in an electric field.
questions.explanation: Cathode rays are streams of electrons, so they consist of tiny negatively charged particles and statement i is correct. Because electrons are charged, cathode rays are deflected by both electric and magnetic fields, so statement ii is false. They are not neutrons, and neutrons are uncharged, so statement iii is also false. Therefore only statement i is correct, giving option 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Natural radioactivity is the random spontaneous disintegration of the nuclei of heavy isotopes of certain elements with the emission of
questions.explanation: Natural radioactivity is the spontaneous decay of unstable nuclei accompanied by emission of alpha particles, beta particles, and gamma rays. X-rays are not the standard emissions from radioactive decay; they usually arise from electron transitions or deceleration processes outside the nucleus. Therefore the only fully correct option is the one containing alpha, beta, and gamma rays. Option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following are produced after a nuclear fusion process? i. one heavy nucleus. ii. neutrons-1. iii. protons. iv. Energy.
questions.explanation: Nuclear fusion is the combination of light nuclei to form a heavier nucleus with the release of energy due to mass defect. Therefore statement i is generally correct and statement iv is also correct. Free neutrons may appear in some fusion reactions, but not in all, so statement ii is not universally valid. Statement iii is likewise not a defining general product. Option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An element X of an atomic number 88 and mass number 226 decays to form an element Z by emitting two beta particles and an alpha particle. Z is represented by
questions.explanation: Start with mass number 226 and atomic number 88. Emission of one alpha particle reduces the mass number by 4 and the atomic number by 2, giving 222 and 86. Each beta minus particle leaves the mass number unchanged but increases the atomic number by 1. After two beta emissions, the atomic number becomes 88 again. The final nucleus is therefore 222 over 88, which is option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The kinetic theory of photoelectron liberated from a metallic surface depends on the
options: time duration of the incident radiation
questions.explanation: The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons is given by Einstein's photoelectric equation: K_max = hf minus work function. This shows that the kinetic energy depends on the frequency of the incident radiation. Intensity mainly affects the number of emitted electrons, provided the frequency is above threshold, while duration and temperature are not the controlling factors here. Therefore option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: What is the least possible error in using a rule graduated in centimeters?
questions.explanation: A rule graduated in centimeters has its smallest marked division equal to 1 cm. For an analog scale, the least possible reading error is taken as half the smallest division because the reading can lie anywhere between adjacent marks. Half of 1 cm is 0.5 cm. Therefore the correct choice is the option giving 0.5 cm, which is at zero-based index 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following affects the period of a simple pendulum? i. mass of the pendulum bob. ii. length of the pendulum. iii. acceleration due to gravity.
questions.explanation: For a simple pendulum undergoing small oscillations, the period is T = 2 pi square root of L/g. This expression shows that the period depends on the length of the pendulum and the local gravitational acceleration, but not on the mass of the bob. Therefore statements ii and iii are correct while statement i is false. Option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A boy sits in a train moving with uniform speed on a straight track. If from his outstretched palm he gently tosses his coin upwards, the coin will fall
questions.explanation: When the coin is tossed, it already has the same horizontal velocity as the train and the boy's hand. Because the train moves at uniform speed in a straight line, there is no horizontal acceleration to change that shared motion. The coin therefore returns to the same horizontal position relative to the boy and falls back into his palm. Option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A body starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of 6 ms \(^{-2}\). What distance does it cover in the third seconds
questions.explanation: Starting from rest with uniform acceleration, the distance covered in the nth second is a(2n minus 1)/2 when initial velocity is zero. With a = 6 m s^-2 and n = 3, the distance in the third second is 6 x 5/2 = 15 m. The same result follows from s at 3 s minus s at 2 s. Therefore option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A stone, Q is thrown with velocity U at an angle of 75o to the horizontal. Another stone R is thrown with the same velocity U but with an angle of 15o to the horizontal. The ranges covered by the stones will be
options: the same for Q and R
greater for the heavier of the two stones
questions.explanation: For a projectile launched and landing at the same level, the range is R = U^2 sin 2 theta over g. For 75 degrees, sin 150 degrees = 1/2. For 15 degrees, sin 30 degrees = 1/2. Since both stones have the same speed U and the same sine factor, their ranges are equal. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A man weight 800N climbs up a stairs to height of 15m in 12.5s. What is the man''s average power output?
questions.explanation: Average power is work done divided by time. The work done in climbing is gain in gravitational potential energy, equal to weight times height: 800 x 15 = 12000 J. Dividing by 12.5 s gives 12000/12.5 = 960 W. The unit is watt because one watt equals one joule per second. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A machine requires 1000J of work to raise a load of 500N through a vertical distance of 1.5m. Calculate the efficiency of the
questions.explanation: Efficiency equals useful output work divided by input work, multiplied by 100 percent. The useful output in lifting the load is 500 x 1.5 = 750 J. The machine requires 1000 J input, so efficiency = 750/1000 x 100 percent = 75 percent. This means three quarters of the supplied work becomes useful lifting work. Option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In an experiment to determine Young's Modulus for a wire, several loads are attached to the wire and the corresponding extension measured. The tensile stress in each case depends on the
options: load and the radius of the wire
radius of the wire and the extension
extension and the original length of the wire
questions.explanation: Tensile stress is defined as force divided by cross-sectional area. For a wire, the area is pi r^2, so the stress depends on the applied load and the wire radius. Extension and original length are used when calculating strain, not stress itself. Therefore the correct factors are the load and the radius of the wire. Option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If a plastic sphere floats in water (density = 1000kgm3) with 0.5 of its volume submerged, and floats in oil with 0.4 of its volume submerged the density of the oil is
questions.explanation: For a floating object, weight equals upthrust, so the fraction submerged equals density of the object divided by density of the liquid. In water, 0.5 = density of sphere over 1000, giving sphere density 500 kg m^-3. In oil, 0.4 = 500 over density of oil, so density of oil = 500/0.4 = 1250 kg m^-3. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A platinum resistance thermometer wire has a resistance of 5 ohms at 0oC and 5.5 ohms at 100oC. Calculate the temperature of the wire when the resistance is 5.2 ohms
questions.explanation: Assuming resistance varies linearly with temperature, the resistance rises from 5.0 ohms at 0 degrees Celsius to 5.5 ohms at 100 degrees Celsius, an increase of 0.5 ohm over 100 degrees. That is 0.005 ohm per degree. A resistance of 5.2 ohms is 0.2 ohm above the 0 degree value, so the temperature is 0.2/0.005 = 40 degrees Celsius. Option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A bridge made of steel is 600m long. What is the daily variation in its length if the night-time and daytime temperatures are 10°C and 35°C respectively. The linear expansivity of steel is 0.000012C\(^{-1}\).
questions.explanation: Use linear expansion: change in length = alpha L delta T. Here alpha = 0.000012 per degree Celsius, L = 600 m, and delta T = 35 minus 10 = 25 degrees. So the change is 0.000012 x 600 x 25 = 0.18 m. Converting to centimetres gives 18 cm. Therefore the daily variation in length is 18.00 cm, which is option 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: One of the most important applications of bi-metallic strip is found in the construction of
questions.explanation: A bimetallic strip bends when its two bonded metals expand by different amounts on heating. This bending is used to open or close an electrical contact automatically at a chosen temperature. That is the operating principle of a thermostat. An altimeter, thermocouple, and hydrometer rely on different physical effects. Therefore the correct application is a thermostat, option 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: At constant pressure, the density of a fixed mass of gas is
questions.explanation: At constant pressure, a fixed mass of gas obeys Charles's law, so its volume is directly proportional to absolute temperature. Density is mass divided by volume, and the mass is fixed, so density is inversely proportional to volume. Therefore density is inversely proportional to absolute temperature as well. This matches option 2, which is the intended answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: How much heat is absorbed when a block of copper of mass 0.05kg and specific heat capacity 390Jkg-1K-1 is heated from 20oC to 70oC?
questions.explanation: Heat absorbed is given by Q = mc delta T. Here m = 0.05 kg, c = 390 J kg^-1 K^-1, and delta T = 70 minus 20 = 50 K. Thus Q = 0.05 x 390 x 50 = 975 J. Written in standard form, 975 J = 9.75 x 10^2 J. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A block of ice floats on water inside a container. If the block of ice gets completely melted, the level of water in the container will
questions.explanation: A floating block of ice displaces a volume of water whose weight equals the weight of the ice. When the ice melts, it becomes exactly the same mass of water, and that meltwater occupies exactly the volume that had been displaced while the ice floated. Therefore there is no change in the water level after melting. Option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The space between the double glass walls of a thermos flask is evacuated space are silvered. The residual source of heat loss takes place by
options: conduction through the stopper and the glass
questions.explanation: In a thermos flask, the vacuum between the double walls prevents convection and greatly reduces conduction across the gap. The silvered surfaces reduce heat transfer by radiation. The remaining important route for heat loss is through the solid materials that still connect the inside and outside, especially the stopper and the supporting glass. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following characteristics of a wave is used in the measurement of the depth of the sea?
questions.explanation: Sea depth is measured by echo sounding. A pulse of sound is sent downward, and the time taken for the returning echo from the seabed is measured. This method depends on reflection of the wave at the bottom surface. Diffraction, interference, and refraction are not the operative feature in the measurement itself. Therefore option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A note is the octave of another note if it has
options: a frequency twice that of the first note
frequency half that of the first note
the same fundamental frequency as the first one
a frequency frequency eight times that of the first note
questions.explanation: An octave means a doubling of frequency. If one note has frequency f, the note one octave above has frequency 2f. A note with frequency f over 2 is an octave below, not above; the same frequency gives the same note; and eight times the frequency corresponds to three octaves above. So the only defensible choice is the first option.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: What is the frequency of the sound made by a siren having a disc with 32 holes and making 25 revolution per seconds?
questions.explanation: In a siren disc, each hole produces one pulse of sound per revolution, so the sound frequency equals holes multiplied by revolutions per second.
