With 32 holes and 25 revolutions each second, the frequency is 32 times 25, which is 800 per second. Since per second is hertz, the correct frequency is 800 Hz, matching option 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following properties make the convex mirror useful as a driving mirror? i. the image is real. ii. the image is erect. iii. it has a wide field of view. iv. the image is magnified.
questions.explanation: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image, and it provides a wide field of view. For driving, the important features are that the image is upright and that more of the road behind can be seen at once. The image is not real and not magnified. Therefore only statements ii and iii are correct, which is option 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When an object is placed very close to the pole of a concave mirror, the virtual image obtained is
questions.explanation: For a concave mirror, when the object is placed between the pole and the principal focus, reflected rays diverge and their backward extensions meet behind the mirror. The image formed is therefore virtual, upright, and magnified. Since the question asks about the virtual image obtained when the object is very close to the pole, the correct description is enlarged and upright, which is option 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A concave mirror has a radius of curvature of 36cm. At what distance from the mirror should an object be placed to give a real image three times the size of the object?
questions.explanation: The focal length of the concave mirror is half the radius of curvature, so f equals 36 over 2, giving 18 cm. A real image three times the object means magnification magnitude equals 3, so v equals 3u. Using 1 over f equals 1 over u plus 1 over v gives 1 over 18 equals 1 over u plus 1 over 3u, hence u equals 24 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The speed of light in air is 3 x 10\(^8\)ms\(^{-1}\). What is the speed in glass with a refractive index of 1.50?
questions.explanation: Refractive index is defined by n equals c over v, where c is the speed of light in air or vacuum and v is the speed in the medium. Rearranging gives v equals c over n. Substituting c equals 3.0 times 10 to the power 8 metres per second and n equals 1.50 gives 2.0 times 10 to the power 8 metres per second. That is option 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If the refractive index of a medium in air is 2.0, what is the critical angle for this medium?
questions.explanation: For light passing from a denser medium to air, the critical angle C satisfies sine C equals 1 over n. With refractive index 2.0, sine C equals 0.5. The angle whose sine is 0.5 is 30 degrees. This result is exact, not approximate, so the correct option is 0. The physical meaning is the incidence angle at which the refracted ray just grazes the boundary.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following arrangements of the components of electromagnetic spectrum is in ascending order of wavelengths?
options: Gamma rays, ultraviolet rays, X- rays, infra - red rays
Gamma rays, X-rays, ultraviolet rays, infra-red rays
infra-red rays, ultraviolet rays, X-rays, gamma rays
Gamma rays, ultraviolet rays, infra-red rays, X-rays
questions.explanation: Wavelength in the electromagnetic spectrum increases from gamma rays to X rays to ultraviolet to visible to infrared, then onward to microwaves and radio waves. Restricting attention to the listed groups, the ascending order of wavelength is gamma rays, X rays, ultraviolet rays, and infra red rays. Any order placing ultraviolet before X rays is incorrect. Therefore option 1 is the correct arrangement.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The angle between the direction of the earth's magnetic field and the horizontal is called the
questions.explanation: The angle between the Earth’s magnetic field direction and the horizontal plane is called the angle of dip, also known as magnetic inclination. Magnetic declination is a different angle: it is the horizontal angle between true north and magnetic north. Magnetic meridian is a direction, not an angle. Therefore the correct term requested here is angle of dip, which is option 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Calculate the force acting on an electron of charge 1.6 x 10-19C placed in an electric field of intensity 108Vm-1
questions.explanation: The electric force on a charge in a uniform electric field is F equals qE. Using q equals 1.6 times 10 to the power minus 19 coulomb and E equals 10 to the power 8 volt per metre, the force is 1.6 times 10 to the power minus 11 newton. The exponent comes from adding minus 19 and 8. This matches option 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When an ebolite rod is rubbed with fur, it has
questions.explanation: When an ebonite rod is rubbed with fur, electrons are transferred from the fur to the rod. The rod gains excess electrons and therefore acquires a net negative charge. It is not left neutral, and although positive and negative charges exist internally, the rod’s overall charge is negative. So the correct choice is option 1. The question’s spelling does not affect the physics.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following factors has no effect on the e.m.f. of a primary cell?
questions.explanation: The e.m.f. of a primary cell depends on the chemical nature of the electrodes, the electrolyte, and temperature because these affect the chemical potential difference. The physical size of the cell mainly changes capacity and internal resistance, not the e.m.f. itself. Therefore the factor with no effect on the e.m.f. is the size of the cell, which corresponds to option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A wire of length 15m made of a material of resistivity 1.8 x 10-6\(\Omega\)m has a resistance of 0.27\(\Omega\). Determine the area of the wire
questions.explanation: For a uniform wire, resistance is given by R equals rho L over A, so area A equals rho L over R. Substituting rho equals 1.8 times 10 to the power minus 6 ohm metre, L equals 15 metres, and R equals 0.27 ohm gives A equals 27 times 10 to the power minus 6 divided by 0.27, which is 1.0 times 10 to the power minus 4 square metre. That is option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A 5-v battery is connected across the plates of a 2.0\(\mu\)F uncharged parallel plate capacitor. The charge on the capacitor after a long time is
questions.explanation: The charge stored on a capacitor is Q equals CV after it has fully charged. Here C equals 2.0 microfarad and V equals 5 volt, so Q equals 2.0 times 10 to the power minus 6 multiplied by 5, giving 10 times 10 to the power minus 6 coulomb. That is 10.0 microcoulomb. The phrase after a long time confirms the capacitor has reached its final charge. Option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following apparatus will require the smallest fuse rating for its protection?
questions.explanation: The fuse rating should exceed the normal operating current, so the apparatus drawing the smallest current needs the smallest fuse. Using I equals P over V gives currents of 0.25 A, 1.5 A, about 3.33 A, and 8 A for the four options respectively. The smallest is 0.25 A for the 60 W, 240 V appliance. Therefore option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The heat produced in a conductor carrying an electric current is
options: inversely proportional to the current and the resistance
directly proportional to the current, resistance and the time
inversely proportional to of the resistance, current and the time
directly proportional to the square of the current, the resistance and the time
questions.explanation: Joule’s law states that the heat produced in a conductor carrying current is H equals I squared R t. This means the heat is directly proportional to the square of the current, the resistance, and the time for which current flows. Any statement with only first power of current is incomplete or wrong. Therefore the correct option is 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The maximum permissible current through a galvanometer G of internal resistance 10\(\Omega\) is 0.05A. A resistance R is used to convert G into a voltmeter with a maximum reading of 100V. Find the value of R and how it is connected to G
questions.explanation: To make a voltmeter from a galvanometer, a large resistance is added in series so that only the galvanometer’s full-scale current flows at the maximum voltage. With V equals 100 V, galvanometer current 0.05 A, and internal resistance 10 ohm, total resistance needed is 100 divided by 0.05, which is 2000 ohm. The added resistance is therefore 2000 minus 10, giving 1990 ohm in series. Option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In alternating current theory, the units of impedance, r.m.s. voltage and resonance frequency are respectively equal to
questions.explanation: Impedance measures opposition to alternating current and has the unit ohm. Root mean square voltage is still a voltage, so its unit is volt. Resonance frequency is a frequency and is measured in hertz. Matching these standard units in order gives ohms, volt, and hertz. Therefore the correct option is 1. No special convention changes any of these units here.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In A.C circuit theory, the root means square (r.m.s) current, Irms and the peak (maximum)current Io are related by
questions.explanation: For a sinusoidal alternating current, the root mean square value equals the peak value divided by the square root of 2. Thus Irms equals Io over square root of 2, while the peak current is square root of 2 times Irms. The other options either invert the relation or are algebraically meaningless. Therefore the correct option is 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The threshold of frequency for photoelectric effect depends on the
options: potential difference between the cathode and the anode
questions.explanation: The threshold frequency in the photoelectric effect is the minimum frequency needed to liberate electrons from the surface. It is linked to the work function by hf0 equals work function. Since the work function depends on the emitting material, the threshold frequency depends on the material of the photocathode. It does not depend on light intensity or the external potential difference. Hence option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: After three half lifes, the fraction of a radioactive material that has decayed is
questions.explanation: After each half life, the undecayed fraction is halved. After three half lives, the remaining fraction is one half cubed, which equals one eighth. Therefore the fraction that has decayed is one minus one eighth, giving seven eighths. This is a straightforward decay fraction calculation and matches option 3 exactly.

questions.subject: physics
questions.explanation: Conserve both mass number and atomic number. On the left, the total mass number is 27 plus 1, giving 28, and the total atomic number is 13. Sodium-24 contributes mass number 24 and atomic number 11, so the missing particle must have mass number 4 and atomic number 2. That particle is a helium nucleus, also called an alpha particle. Therefore option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is the most suitable for use as an altimeter?
questions.explanation: An altimeter works by relating atmospheric pressure to height. The most suitable instrument is an aneroid barometer because it is compact, does not rely on a liquid column, and can be used conveniently in aircraft and field instruments. Mercury barometers and manometers are bulky and less practical for this purpose. Therefore the best choice is option 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A body of weight W N rest on a smooth plane inclined at an angle\(\theta\)o to the horizontal. What is the resolved part of the weight in Newtons along the plane?
questions.explanation: For a plane inclined at angle theta to the horizontal, the weight W resolves into two components: one perpendicular to the plane and one parallel to it. The component acting down the plane is W sine theta, while the normal component is W cosine theta. Since the question asks for the resolved part along the plane, the correct expression is W sine theta, which is option 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A small metal ball thrown vertically upwards from the top of a tower with an initial velocity of 20ms-1. If the ball took a total of 6s to reach ground level, determine the height of the tower [g = 10ms-2]
questions.explanation: Take upward as positive with initial velocity 20 metres per second, acceleration minus 10 metres per second squared, and time 6 seconds. The displacement after 6 seconds is s equals ut plus one half at squared, giving 20 times 6 plus one half times minus 10 times 36, which is 120 minus 180 equals minus 60 metres. The negative sign means the ground is 60 metres below the release point, so the tower is 60 m high.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An object moves with uniform speed round a circle. Its acceleration has
questions.explanation: In uniform circular motion, the speed is constant, so the centripetal acceleration has constant magnitude v squared over r as long as v and r stay constant. However, its direction is always toward the centre of the circle, and that inward direction changes continuously as the object moves around. Therefore the acceleration has constant magnitude and varying direction, which is option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A body of mass 100g moving with a velocity of 10.0ms-1 collides with a wall. If after collision, it moves with a velocity of 2.0ms-1 in the opposite direction, calculate the change in momentum.
questions.explanation: Momentum change is final momentum minus initial momentum. The mass is 100 g, which is 0.1 kg. Taking the initial velocity as plus 10.0 metres per second and the final velocity as minus 2.0 metres per second because the ball rebounds, delta p equals 0.1 times minus 2 minus 10, which is minus 1.2 kilogram metre per second. Its magnitude is 1.2 newton second, matching option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A spring of force constant 1500Nm-1 is acted upon by a constant force of 75N. Calculate the potential energy stored in the string
questions.explanation: For a spring obeying Hooke’s law, F equals kx, so the extension is x equals 75 over 1500, which is 0.05 m. The elastic potential energy stored is one half kx squared. Substituting gives one half times 1500 times 0.05 squared, which equals 1.875 J. Rounded to one decimal place, this is 1.9 J. Therefore option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A wheel and axle have radii 80cm and 10cm respectively. If the efficiency of the machine is 0.85, an applied force of 1200N to the wheel will raise a load of
questions.explanation: For a wheel and axle, the velocity ratio is wheel radius divided by axle radius, so 80 over 10 equals 8. Efficiency equals mechanical advantage divided by velocity ratio, hence mechanical advantage is 0.85 times 8, which is 6.8. Since mechanical advantage equals load over effort, the load is 6.8 times 1200 N, giving 8160 N. Therefore the correct option is 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A 20kg mass is to be pulled up a slope inclined at 30o to the horizontal. If the efficiency of the plane is 75%, the force required to pull the load up the plane is [g = 10ms-2]
questions.explanation: The load weighs mg equals 20 times 10, so its weight is 200 N. For an inclined plane at 30 degrees, the velocity ratio is length over height, which equals 1 over sine 30 degrees, giving 2. With efficiency 75 percent, mechanical advantage equals 0.75 times 2, which is 1.5. Effort equals load over mechanical advantage, so effort is 200 over 1.5, giving 133.3 N. Hence option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The spiral spring of a spring balance is 25.0cm long when 5N hangs on it and 30cm long, when the weight is 10N. What is the length of the spring if the weight is 3N assuming Hooke's law is obeyed?
questions.explanation: Under Hooke’s law, equal additional forces produce equal additional extensions. Increasing the load from 5 N to 10 N increases the spring length from 25 cm to 30 cm, so 5 N produces 5 cm extra extension and 1 N produces 1 cm. Therefore the natural length is 25 minus 5, which is 20 cm. With a 3 N load, the extension is 3 cm, so the length is 23 cm. Option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The mass of a stone is 15.0g when completely immersed in water and 10.0g when completely immersed in a liquid of relative density 2.0. The mass of the stone in air is
questions.explanation: Let the mass in air be M grams. In water, the apparent loss is M minus 15. In a liquid of relative density 2.0, the upthrust is twice that in water, so M minus 10 equals 2 times M minus 15. Solving gives M minus 10 equals 2M minus 30, hence M equals 20 g. Therefore the mass of the stone in air is 20.0 g, which is option 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In which of the following is surface tension important?
options: the floating of a ship in water
the floating of a dry needle in water
the floating of a baloon in air
the diffusion of sugar solution across a membrane
questions.explanation: Surface tension is important when a small object is supported by the stretched surface layer of a liquid. A dry needle can float on water for this reason if placed carefully. A ship floats mainly because of buoyancy, a balloon in air because of upthrust in a gas, and diffusion across a membrane because of concentration differences. Therefore the correct example is the floating of a dry needle in water, option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A thermometer with an arbitrary scale S, of equal division registers -30oS at the ice point and +90oS at the steam point. Calculate the Celsius temperature corresponding to 60oS
questions.explanation: Because the arbitrary scale has equal divisions, its relation to Celsius is linear. Ice point gives minus 30 degrees S corresponding to 0 degrees C, and steam point gives 90 degrees S corresponding to 100 degrees C. A reading of 60 degrees S is 90 S-divisions above ice point out of a total span of 120 divisions, so the Celsius temperature is 90 over 120 times 100, which equals 75 degrees C. Option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A brass rod is 2m long at a certain temperature. What is the length for a temperature rise of 100K, if the expansivity of brass is 18 x 10-6K-1?
questions.explanation: Linear expansion is given by delta L equals alpha L delta T. Here alpha equals 18 times 10 to the power minus 6 per kelvin, L equals 2 m, and delta T equals 100 K. So delta L equals 18 times 10 to the power minus 6 times 2 times 100, which is 0.0036 m. The new length is 2.0000 plus 0.0036, giving 2.0036 m. That matches option 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: What is the difference in the amount of heat given out by 4kg of steam and 4kg of water when both are cooled from 100ºC to 80ºC? [the specific latent heat of steam is 2,260,000Jkg\(^{-1}\), specific heat capacity of water is 4200Jkg\(^{-1}\)K\(^{-1}\)]
questions.explanation: Four kilograms of steam at 100 degrees Celsius must first condense to water at 100 degrees Celsius, then the resulting water cools to 80 degrees Celsius. Four kilograms of water at 100 degrees Celsius only cools to 80 degrees Celsius. Since both release the same sensible heat during cooling, the difference is only the latent heat of condensation: 4 times 2,260,000 J, which equals 9,040,000 J. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: How long does it take a 750W heater to raise the temperature of 1kg of water from 20oC to 50oC [specific heat capacity of water = 4200Jkg-1K-1]
questions.explanation: The heat needed is mc delta T. For 1 kg of water heated through 30 K, the energy required is 1 times 4200 times 30, which equals 126000 J. A 750 W heater supplies 750 J each second, so the time is energy divided by power: 126000 divided by 750 equals 168 s. Therefore the correct option is 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The saturated vapour pressure of a liquid increases as the
questions.explanation: Saturated vapour pressure is the equilibrium pressure of vapour above a liquid. As temperature increases, more molecules have enough energy to escape the liquid, so the equilibrium vapour pressure rises. It is not primarily determined by the volume of the liquid in the container, provided liquid and vapour are both present. Therefore the correct statement is that it increases as the temperature increases, which is option 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The absolute temperature of a perfect gas is proportional to the average
questions.explanation: According to kinetic theory, the absolute temperature of a perfect gas is proportional to the average translational kinetic energy of its molecules. It is not proportional to molecular separation or potential energy, and not directly proportional to velocity because kinetic energy depends on the square of speed. Therefore the correct option is 2, kinetic energy of the molecules.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A room is heated by means of a charcoal fire, An occupant of the room standing away from the fire is warmed mainly by
questions.explanation: A person standing away from a charcoal fire is warmed mainly by thermal radiation traveling directly from the hot source to the body. Conduction requires contact, so it is negligible here. Convection mainly carries hot air upward and does not account for the dominant direct warming at a distance. Reflection is secondary, not the main heat-transfer mechanism from the fire. Thus option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A boy timed 30 oscillations of a certain pendulum thrice and obtained 1min. 10s, 1min. 12s and 1min. 7s respectively.The mean period of oscillation of the pendulum is
questions.explanation: The three times for 30 oscillations are 70 s, 72 s, and 67 s. Their mean is 209 over 3 seconds, which is 69.67 s approximately. The period is the time for one oscillation, so divide by 30: 69.67 over 30 equals about 2.32 s. Therefore the mean period is 2.32 s, matching option 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is TRUE of light and sound waves?
options: they both need a mediumfor propagation
their velocities in air are equal
questions.explanation: Both light and sound transport energy from one place to another, so that statement is true. Sound requires a material medium, but light does not, so option 1 is false. Light is transverse while sound in air is longitudinal, so option 2 is false. Their speeds in air are vastly different, making option 3 false. Therefore option 0 is the only correct statement.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The image in a pin-hole camera is
options: errect and formed by refraction through a lens
erect and gets sharper as the hole becomes larger
inverted and formed by the light from each point travelling in a straight line
questions.explanation: A pin-hole camera forms its image because light travels in straight lines. Rays from the top and bottom of the object cross at the tiny aperture and fall on opposite parts of the screen, producing an inverted image. No lens or refraction is involved, and enlarging the hole makes the image less sharp, not sharper. Therefore option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When a plane mirror at which a ray is incident is rotated through an angle \( \theta \), the reflected ray will be rotated through
questions.explanation: When a plane mirror rotates through an angle theta, its normal also rotates through theta. Since the reflected ray must remain at the same angle to the new normal as the incident ray makes with it, the reflected direction changes by twice the mirror’s rotation. This is a standard consequence of the law of reflection. Hence the reflected ray rotates through 2 theta, which is option 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A trough 12.0cm deep is filled with water of refractive index \(\frac{4}{3}\). By how much would a coin at the bottom of the trough appear to be displaced when viewed vertically from above the water surface?
questions.explanation: Viewed vertically from air, an object under water appears shallower than its real depth. Apparent depth equals real depth divided by refractive index, so it is 12.0 divided by 4 over 3, which gives 9.0 cm. The apparent upward displacement is the difference between real and apparent depth: 12.0 minus 9.0 equals 3.0 cm. Therefore option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following correctly, describes the image of an object, 4cm from a diverging lens of focal length 12cm?
options: The image is virtual, 3cm in front of the lens
The image is real, 6cm behind the lens
The image is virtual, 6cm in front of the lens
The image is real, 3cm in front the lens
questions.explanation: A diverging lens has negative focal length. Using the Cartesian sign convention, f equals minus 12 cm and u equals minus 4 cm. The lens formula 1 over f equals 1 over v minus 1 over u gives minus 1 over 12 equals 1 over v plus 1 over 4, so 1 over v equals minus 1 over 3 and v equals minus 3 cm. Negative v means a virtual image 3 cm in front of the lens. Option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Two tuning forks of frequency 256Hz and 260Hz are sounded close to each other. What is the frequency of the beats produced?
questions.explanation: Beat frequency is the absolute difference between the two sound frequencies. For 256 Hz and 260 Hz, the difference is 4 Hz. This value represents how many loudness maxima are heard each second when the tuning forks sound together. It is not the average or sum of the frequencies. Therefore the correct option is 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A man hears his echo from a nearby hill 2s after he shouted. If the frequency of his voice is 260Hz and the wavelength is 1.29m, how far away is the hill?
questions.explanation: The speed of sound is found from v equals f lambda. With frequency 260 Hz and wavelength 1.29 m, v equals 260 times 1.29, giving 335.4 metres per second. The 2 s echo time is for the round trip to the hill and back, so the one-way travel time is 1 s. Distance to the hill is therefore 335.4 times 1, which is 335.4 m. Option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When the bottom tip of a vibrating tuning fork is held in contact with a wooden box, a louder sound is heard. This phenomenon is known as
questions.explanation: The louder sound is due to resonance. The tuning fork forces the wooden box to vibrate at the same frequency, and if the box can respond strongly, the vibration amplitude of the box becomes much larger, so more air is set into motion and the sound is amplified. Beats need two nearby frequencies, echoing is reflected sound, and reverberation is prolonged multiple reflection of sound.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following statements is CORRECT about the earth's magnetic field?
options: the angle of dip is the angle which a freely suspended magnet makes with the vertical
the angle of declination is the angle between the magnetic meridian and the geographic meridian
the angle of declination is the angle which a magnetic compass makes with the magnetic meridian
the angle of inclination is the difference between the angle of dip and the angle of declination
questions.explanation: The correct statement is that angle of declination is the angle between the geographic meridian and the magnetic meridian. Angle of dip, also called inclination, is the angle the Earth's magnetic field makes with the horizontal, not with the vertical. A compass needle aligns with the magnetic meridian rather than making an angle with it. So only option 1 matches the standard definitions.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The function of the system of granulated carbon mixed with manganese (IV) oxide in a Letanche cell is to
options: increase the e.m.f. of the cell to 2.0V
prevent local action in the cell
make the cell black and hence a good radiator
questions.explanation: In a Leclanche cell, hydrogen tends to collect at the cathode during use. This coating reduces the cell's effectiveness and lowers the current, a problem called polarization. The mixture of granulated carbon and manganese(IV) oxide acts as a depolarizer by removing the hydrogen effect. It does not raise the e.m.f. to 2.0 V, prevent local action, or serve any thermal radiation purpose. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A moving coil galvanometer of 300\(\Omega\) resistance gives full scale deflection for 1.0mA. The resistance R, of the shunt that is required to convert the galvanometer into a 3.0A ammeter is
questions.explanation: At full-scale deflection the galvanometer carries 0.001 A through 300 ohms, so the voltage across it is V = IG = 0.001 x 300 = 0.3 V. To read 3.0 A as an ammeter, the shunt carries 3.0 - 0.001 = 2.999 A at the same 0.3 V. Hence R = V over Ish = 0.3 divided by 2.999, about 0.10 ohm. So option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An equipment whose power is 1500W and resistance is 375 ohms would draw a current of
questions.explanation: Use P = I squared R. With P = 1500 W and R = 375 ohms, I squared = 1500 divided by 375 = 4. Taking the positive square root gives I = 2 A. This is consistent with power in watts and resistance in ohms giving current in amperes. Therefore the equipment draws 2.00 A, which corresponds to option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: To convert an alternating current dynamo into a direct current dynamo, the
options: number of turns in the coil is increased
strength of the field magnet is increased
slip rings are replaced with a split ring commutator
coil is wound on a soft iron armature
questions.explanation: An alternating-current dynamo uses slip rings, so the external connections preserve the alternating polarity generated in the rotating coil. To obtain direct current, the external connection must reverse every half turn so that the current in the outside circuit remains in one direction. That is done by replacing the slip rings with a split-ring commutator. Changes in turns, field strength, or armature material do not perform this conversion.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The electrochemical equivalent of platinum is 5.0 x 10-7kgC-1 to plate-out 1.0kg of platinum, a current of 100A must be passed through an appropriate vessel for
questions.explanation: For electrolysis, deposited mass satisfies m = ZIt, where Z is the electrochemical equivalent in kilograms per coulomb. Substituting m = 1.0 kg, Z = 5.0 x 10^-7 kg C^-1, and I = 100 C s^-1 gives t = 1.0 divided by 5.0 x 10^-5 = 2.0 x 10^4 s. Converting to hours, 20000 divided by 3600 is about 5.6 hours, so option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: which of the following statements are TRUE of isotopes? i. isotopes of an element have the same chemical properties because they have the same number of electrons. ii. isotopes of elements are normally separated using physical properties. iii. isotopes of an element have the same number of protons in their nuclei.
questions.explanation: All three statements are true. Isotopes are atoms of the same element, so they have the same number of protons, making statement iii true. For neutral atoms, that also means the same number of electrons and therefore essentially the same chemical properties, so i is true. Because isotopes differ in mass and related physical behavior, they are commonly separated by physical methods, making ii true as well.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When an atom loses or gains a charge, it becomes
questions.explanation: A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons. If it loses electrons, it becomes positively charged; if it gains electrons, it becomes negatively charged. In either case it is no longer neutral and is called an ion. It does not become an electron, neutron, or proton, because those are individual subatomic particles rather than charged atoms.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: 4g of a radioactive material of half-life 10 days is spilled on a laboratory floor. How long would it take to disintegrate 3.5g of the material?
questions.explanation: If 3.5 g disintegrates from an initial 4.0 g, the mass left is 0.5 g. With a half-life of 10 days, the sample goes from 4.0 g to 2.0 g in 10 days, to 1.0 g in 20 days, and to 0.5 g in 30 days. That is three half-lives. Therefore the required time is 30 days, so option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In a nuclear fusion process, four protons each of mass Mp were fused to produce a nucleus X of mass Mx. Which of the following equations is CORRECT?
questions.explanation: In fusion, the final nucleus has less mass than the total mass of the separate particles that formed it. The missing mass appears as binding energy according to mass-energy equivalence. Therefore if four protons each of mass Mp fuse to produce nucleus X of mass Mx, the correct relation is 4Mp greater than Mx. This makes option 0 the correct choice.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following are True for \(\alpha\)-decay. i. mass number, decrease by four. ii. Atomic number decreases by two. iii. mass number does not change.
questions.explanation: An alpha particle is a helium nucleus containing two protons and two neutrons. When a nucleus emits one alpha particle, its mass number decreases by 4 and its atomic number decreases by 2. So statements i and ii are true, while statement iii is false because the mass number certainly changes. Hence the correct combination is i and ii only, which is option 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following phenomena is called photoelectric effect?
options: high energy electrons impinge on a metalic anode which then emits photons
a high energy photon emits photons as it slowed down
a metal absorbs quanta of light and then emits electrons
Two electrons are created from a quantum of light
questions.explanation: The photoelectric effect is the emission of electrons from a metal surface when light of sufficiently high frequency falls on it. So the correct description is that a metal absorbs light quanta and then emits electrons. High-energy electrons striking a target describe X-ray production, and creating two particles from a photon refers to pair production. Therefore option 2 is the correct interpretation.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is a fundamental unit?
questions.explanation: The second is an SI base unit, used for measuring time. Newton, joule, and watt are all derived units: a newton is force, a joule is energy, and a watt is power. Since the question asks for a fundamental unit, only second qualifies. Therefore the correct option is 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A car moving with a speed of 90kmh\(^{-1}\) was brought uniformly to rest by the application of the brakes in 10s. How far did the car travel after the brakes were applied?
questions.explanation: First convert 90 km per hour to metres per second: 90 x 1000 divided by 3600 = 25 m/s. The car slows uniformly to rest in 10 s, so the average speed during braking is 25 plus 0 over 2, which is 12.5 m/s. Distance traveled equals average speed times time, giving 12.5 x 10 = 125 m. Therefore option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A particle of mass M which is at rest splits up into two. If the mass and velocity of one of the particles are m and v respectively, calculate the velocity of the second particle
questions.explanation: The initial particle is at rest, so total momentum before splitting is zero. After splitting, one fragment has momentum mv. The other fragment must therefore have equal magnitude of momentum in the opposite direction. If its mass is M - m and its speed is u, then (M - m)u = mv. Hence u = mv divided by M - m, opposite in direction to the first fragment. Option 3 gives the correct speed.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct about an object in equilibrium under parallel forces? i. the total clockwise moments of the forces about any point equals the total anti-clockwise moments about the same point. ii. the total forces in one direction equals the total forces in the opposite direction. iii. the resolved components along the x-axis equals the resolved components along the y-axis.
questions.explanation: For equilibrium under parallel forces, two conditions must hold: the total clockwise moment about any point equals the total anticlockwise moment about that point, and the total force in one direction equals the total force in the opposite direction. Statement iii is false because x-components do not have to equal y-components; rather the resultant along each axis must be zero separately. Therefore i and ii only are correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: To keep a vehicle moving at a constant speed v, requires power P, from the engine. The force provided by the engine is
questions.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work, and for a constant driving force acting in the direction of motion, P = Fv. Rearranging gives F = P divided by v. This has the correct dimensions because watt divided by metre per second equals newton. The alternative expressions do not have the correct form for force. Therefore option 0 is the correct answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A stone of mass m kg is held h meters above the floor for 50s. The work done in joules over this period is
questions.explanation: Work done equals force multiplied by displacement in the direction of the force. While the stone is being held stationary for 50 s, its displacement is zero throughout the interval. Since there is no movement, the mechanical work done on the stone over that time is zero, regardless of how long it is held. Therefore the correct answer is option 3, zero.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A body of mass 10kg rests on a rough inclined plane whose angle of tilt \(\theta\) is variable. \(\theta\) is gradually increased until the body starts to slide down the plane at 30o. The coefficient of limiting friction between the body and the plane
questions.explanation: At the instant the body just begins to slide, friction is limiting, so along the plane mg sin theta equals mu mg cos theta. Hence mu = tan theta. With theta = 30 degrees, mu = tan 30 degrees = 1 over square root of 3, about 0.577. Rounded to two decimal places this is 0.58. The mass cancels out and is irrelevant. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An inclined plane which makes an angle of 30o with the horizontal has a velocity ratio of
questions.explanation: For an ideal inclined plane, velocity ratio equals the distance moved by the effort divided by the distance moved by the load. Geometrically this is the length of the plane divided by the vertical height, which is 1 over sin theta. For theta = 30 degrees, sin 30 degrees = 0.5, so the velocity ratio is 1 divided by 0.5 = 2. Therefore option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: What is the length of liquid column in a barometer tube that would support an atmospheric pressure of 102000Nm-2 if the density of the liquid is 2600kgm-3? [g = 10ms-2]
questions.explanation: A barometer balances atmospheric pressure with liquid pressure, so P = rho gh. Substituting P = 102000 N/m^2, rho = 2600 kg/m^3, and g = 10 m/s^2 gives h = 102000 divided by 26000 = 3.923 m. To three significant figures this is 3.92 m. The units are metres, as required for column length. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: 40m3 of liquid is mixed with 60m3 of another liquid Q. If the density of P and Q are 1.00kgm-3 and 1.6kgm-3 respectively, what is the density of the mixture?
questions.explanation: Density of the mixture is total mass divided by total volume, assuming the volumes add. Mass of P is 1.00 x 40 = 40 kg, and mass of Q is 1.6 x 60 = 96 kg. Total mass is 136 kg and total volume is 100 m^3. Therefore the density of the mixture is 136 divided by 100 = 1.36 kg/m^3. Hence option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The resistances of platinum wire at the ice and steam points are 0.75 ohm and 1.05 ohm respectively. Determine the temperature at which the resistance of the wire is 0.90 ohm
questions.explanation: Assuming resistance varies linearly with temperature over this range, use Rtheta - R0 over R100 - R0 equals theta over 100. Here R0 = 0.75 ohm, R100 = 1.05 ohm, and Rtheta = 0.90 ohm. So theta over 100 = 0.15 over 0.30 = 0.5, giving theta = 50 degrees Celsius. Therefore the correct option is 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A bar of initial length /0 is heated through a temperature change \(\Delta\)t to a new length I. The linear expansivity, a, of the bar is
questions.explanation: Linear expansivity is defined as the increase in length per unit original length per degree rise in temperature. If the original length is l0 and the final length is l, then the extension is l minus l0. Hence alpha equals l minus l0 divided by l0 times delta t. The original length must appear in the denominator, not the final length. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: 1kg of copper is transferred quickly from boiling water to a block of ice. Calculate the mass of ice melted, neglecting heat loss. [specific heat capacity of copper 400Jkg-1K-1 and latent heat of fusion of ice 333 x 103Jkg-1]
questions.explanation: The 1 kg copper cools from 100 degrees Celsius to 0 degrees Celsius, so heat lost is Q = mc delta T = 1 x 400 x 100 = 40000 J. This energy melts ice at 0 degrees Celsius. Using m = Q over L, the mass of ice melted is 40000 divided by 333000 = 0.120 kg, which is 120 g. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following conditions will make water boil at a temperature of 100oC when the atmospheric pressure is 750mmHg?
options: heat more rapidly at the same pressure
reduce the external pressure by a quarter
questions.explanation: Water boils when its vapour pressure equals the external pressure. At standard atmospheric pressure of 760 mmHg, pure water boils at 100 degrees Celsius. Since the given pressure is only 750 mmHg, water would boil at a slightly lower temperature than 100 degrees Celsius. To make the boiling point become exactly 100 degrees Celsius, the external pressure must be increased. So option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct? i. land and sea breezes are natural convection currents. ii. convection may occur in liquids or gasses but not in solids. iii. the vacuum in a thermos flask prevents heat loss due to convection only.
questions.explanation: Statement i is true because land and sea breezes arise from convection currents in air. Statement ii is also true because convection occurs in fluids, namely liquids and gases, but not in solids. Statement iii is false because the vacuum in a thermos flask reduces heat transfer by both conduction and convection, not convection alone. Therefore the correct combination is i and ii only, which is option 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A light wave of frequency 5 x 10\(^{14}\)Hz moves through water which has a refractive index of \(\frac{4}{3}\). Calculate the wavelength in water if the velocity of light in air is 3 x 10\(^8\)ms\(^{-1}\)
questions.explanation: The refractive index n = c over v, so the speed of light in water is v = c over n = 3 x 10^8 divided by 4 over 3 = 2.25 x 10^8 m/s. Frequency does not change on entering water, so f remains 5 x 10^14 Hz. Hence wavelength in water is lambda = v over f = 2.25 x 10^8 divided by 5 x 10^14 = 4.5 x 10^-7 m. Option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A wave disturbance travelling in air enters a medium in which its velocity is less than that in air. Which of the following statements is true about the wave medium?
options: both the frequency of the wave and the wavelength are decreased
the frequency of the wave is decreased while the wavelength is increased
the frequency of the wave is unaltered while the wavelength is decreased
the frequency of the wave is decreased while the wavelength is unaltered
questions.explanation: When a wave enters another medium, its frequency remains fixed because the source determines the frequency. The wave speed, however, depends on the medium. Since the new medium makes the speed smaller, and v = f lambda, the wavelength must also decrease while frequency stays unchanged. Therefore the true statement is that the frequency is unaltered and the wavelength is decreased, which is option 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Shadows and eclipses result from the
questions.explanation: Shadows and eclipses occur because light travels in straight lines in a uniform medium. An opaque object blocks some of those rays, leaving a region into which light does not reach, producing a shadow. The same straight-line propagation explains the alignment responsible for eclipses. Refraction, reflection, and diffraction are different optical effects and are not the primary cause here. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An object which is 3cm high is placed vertically 10cm in front of a concave mirror. If this object produces an image 40cm from the mirror, the height of the image is
questions.explanation: Mirror magnification is image height over object height equals image distance over object distance in magnitude. Here the object height is 3 cm, the object distance is 10 cm, and the image distance is 40 cm. So magnification is 40 divided by 10 = 4. Therefore the image height is 4 x 3 = 12 cm. Hence option 3 is correct. The real image would be inverted, though the question asks only for height.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A boy looks at the image of an object in a plane mirror. He observes two images, a main bright one and the other faint. The observed images result from?
questions.explanation: A common plane mirror is a sheet of glass with a reflecting metallic backing. The bright main image comes from reflection at the silvered back surface. A faint secondary image appears because light is refracted into the glass and also partially reflected at the front glass surface, producing another weaker image. Therefore the two observed images arise from reflection and refraction, not reflection alone. Option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: What must be the distance between an object and a converging lens of focal length 20cm to produce an erect image two times the object height?
questions.explanation: An erect image from a converging lens is virtual, so the object must be inside the focal length. The magnification is 2, so in magnitude v over u = 2, giving v = 2u. For a virtual image, use 1 over f = 1 over u minus 1 over v. Substituting f = 20 cm and v = 2u gives 1 over 20 = 1 over 2u, so u = 10 cm. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: For a short sighted person, light rays from a point on a very distant object is focused
options: on the retina by a converging lens
behind the retina by a diverging lens
in front of the retina, a distance 2F from the lens
questions.explanation: In myopia, or short sight, the eye focuses parallel rays from distant objects before they reach the retina. This happens because the eyeball is too long or the eye lens system is too powerful. As a result, distant objects appear blurred. The defect is corrected with a diverging lens so the image shifts back onto the retina. Therefore option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When light is incident on an object which is magenta in colour, which of the following colour would be absorbed?
questions.explanation: A magenta object appears magenta because under white light it reflects red and blue components and absorbs the complementary component, green. Therefore the color absorbed is green only. If it absorbed red or blue as well, it would not appear magenta. Hence the correct option is 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In a resonance tube experiment, the effective length of the air column for the first resonance is 20cm when set into vibration by a tuning fork of frequency 480Hz. Neglecting and effect, the velocity of sound in air is
questions.explanation: For the first resonance in a tube closed at one end, the effective air-column length is one quarter wavelength, so L = lambda over 4. With L = 20 cm = 0.20 m, lambda = 4L = 0.80 m. The speed of sound is then v = f lambda = 480 x 0.80 = 384 m/s. Since end correction is neglected, no further adjustment is needed. Option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An organic pipe closed at one end is 80cm long. Determine the frequency of the fundamental note assuming that the speed of sound in air is 340ms-1
questions.explanation: A pipe closed at one end has its fundamental mode when the length equals one quarter of the wavelength. Thus lambda = 4L = 4 x 0.80 = 3.20 m. Using f = v over lambda gives f = 340 divided by 3.20 = 106.25 Hz. Rounded to the nearest whole number, this is 106 Hz. Therefore option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A sonometer wire of length 100cm under a tension of 10N, has a frequency of 250Hz. Keeping the length of the wire constant, the tension is adjusted to produce a new frequency of 350Hz. The new tension is
questions.explanation: For a stretched wire of fixed length and fixed linear density, frequency is proportional to the square root of tension. Therefore T2 over T1 = f2 squared over f1 squared. With T1 = 10 N, f1 = 250 Hz, and f2 = 350 Hz, T2 = 10 x 350 over 250 squared = 10 x 1.96 = 19.6 N. Hence option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: One of the properties of the earth's magnetic field is that the
options: north pole lies in the northern hemisphere
earth's magnetic flux is entirely horizontal at a place where the magnetic dip is zero
earth's magnetic flux is entirely vertical at a place where the magnetic dip is zero
questions.explanation: The angle of dip is the angle the Earth's magnetic field makes with the horizontal. If the dip is zero, the field has no vertical component at that place and lies entirely in the horizontal plane. So the Earth's magnetic flux there is entirely horizontal. Geographic and magnetic meridians do not generally coincide, and option 0 is not a reliable statement of field properties. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is a vector?
questions.explanation: Electric field is a vector because at each point it has both magnitude and direction, defined as force per unit positive charge. Electric charge, potential difference, and capacitance do not have directional character and are scalars. Therefore the only vector quantity listed is electric field, which is option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Three cells each of e.m.f. 1.5v and an internal resistance of 1.0\(\Omega\) are connected in parallel across a load resistance of 2.67\(\Omega\). Calculate the current in the load?
questions.explanation: Three identical 1.5 V cells in parallel still provide an e.m.f. of 1.5 V, but their equivalent internal resistance becomes 1.0 divided by 3 = 0.333 ohm. This is in series with the 2.67 ohm load, giving a total resistance of about 3.00 ohms. The circuit current is therefore 1.5 divided by 3.00 = 0.50 A. That same current passes through the load, so option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When a known standard resistor of 2\(\Omega\) is connected to the 0.0cm end of a meter bridge, the balance point is found to be at 55.0cm. What is the value of the unknown resistor?
questions.explanation: In a meter bridge at balance, the ratio of the resistances equals the ratio of the lengths of the wire segments. With the known 2 ohm resistor at the 0 cm end and the balance point at 55 cm, the left and right segments are 55 cm and 45 cm. So 2 over Rx = 55 over 45, giving Rx = 2 x 45 over 55 = 1.64 ohms approximately. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The total energy required to send a unit positive charge round a complete electrical circuit is the
questions.explanation: Electromotive force is the energy supplied by a source per unit positive charge in driving charge round the complete circuit. Potential difference is also energy per unit charge, but it usually refers to two points or a part of a circuit, not the entire source action around the whole loop. Therefore the quantity described in the question is electromotive force, so option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is an essential physical property of the wires used for making fuses?
questions.explanation: A fuse must melt quickly when the current becomes excessive, thereby opening the circuit before damage occurs elsewhere. For that purpose, the most essential property of fuse material is a low melting point. Low density is irrelevant, and high thermal conductivity or low resistivity would not be the defining protective feature. Therefore option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is most suitable for protecting the circuit of 2000W electric iron connected to a 250V mains?
questions.explanation: The iron draws current I = P/V = 2000/250 = 8 A. A protective fuse should be slightly above the normal operating current so that normal use does not melt it, but overload current still does. Among the choices, 8 A is too exact and may blow in service, while 13 A is the next suitable rating. Therefore 13 A is best.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Electrical power is transmitted at a high voltage rather than low voltage because the amount of energy loss is reduced due to
questions.explanation: For a given transmitted power, raising the transmission voltage lowers the current because P = VI. Power lost in the wires is I squared R, so a smaller current greatly reduces heating loss. The reduced energy loss is therefore due to less heat produced in the transmission lines, not eddy currents or any effect of distance. Hence the correct choice is heat dissipation.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A lamp is rated 240V, 60W. The resistance of the filament is
questions.explanation: For a lamp operating at its rated values, P = V squared over R, so R = V squared over P. Using V = 240 V and P = 60 W gives R = 240 squared divided by 60 = 57600 divided by 60 = 960 ohms. The filament resistance is therefore 960 ohms, which matches option 0 exactly.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A 0 - 10mA galvanometer with a coil resistance of 30\(\Omega\) can be converted to a 0 - 10A ammeter by using
questions.explanation: To make a galvanometer read large currents, a small shunt resistor is connected in parallel so most current bypasses the coil. The galvanometer full-scale current is 0.01 A and its resistance is 30 ohms, so the coil p.d. is 0.01 x 30 = 0.3 V. The shunt carries 10 - 0.01 = 9.99 A, giving Rsh = 0.3/9.99 about 0.03 ohms.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The number of neutrons contained in the nucleus \(^{238}_{92}U\) is
questions.explanation: In nuclide notation, the mass number is total nucleons and the atomic number is protons. Neutrons equal mass number minus atomic number. For uranium-238, neutrons = 238 - 92 = 146. This also checks because 92 protons plus 146 neutrons gives 238 nucleons. Therefore the nucleus contains 146 neutrons, corresponding to option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: What precaution should a manufacturer take to ensure that energy loss in a transformer is minimized?
options: the winding of the transformer should be made of high resistance wire
the core should be made of thin sheets of metal
no magnetic material should be used to make the core
the flux linking the primary with the secondary coils should be minimum
questions.explanation: A transformer loses energy mainly through eddy currents and hysteresis in the core and resistance heating in the windings. Laminating the core into thin metal sheets greatly reduces eddy currents by interrupting large circular current paths. High-resistance windings would increase copper loss, and weak flux linkage would make the transformer ineffective. So the correct precaution is to use thin sheets of metal for the core.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A substance has a half of 3mins. after 6mins. the count rate was observed to be 400. What was its count rate at zero time?
questions.explanation: The half-life is 3 minutes, so 6 minutes corresponds to two half-lives. After one half-life the count rate is halved, and after two half-lives it becomes one quarter of the initial value. Thus 400 = initial count divided by 4, so the initial count rate was 400 x 4 = 1600. Option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The photocell works on the principle of the
options: emision of electrons by incident radiation
emision of protons by incident electrons
questions.explanation: A photocell operates by the photoelectric effect. When radiation of sufficiently high frequency falls on a suitable metal surface, electrons are emitted from that surface. It is not based on a voltaic cell, proton emission, or ordinary photographic action. Therefore the correct description is emission of electrons by incident radiation, which is option 1 despite the spelling error in the wording.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is a set of vectors?
questions.explanation: A vector has magnitude and direction. Acceleration and velocity are standard vector quantities. Moment of a force also has directional sense and is treated as a vector quantity in elementary mechanics. Mass, volume, and density are scalars. Therefore the only set consisting entirely of vectors is acceleration, velocity and moment, which is option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The magnitude of the resultant of two mutually perpendicular forces, F1 and F2 is 13N, if the magnitude of F1 is 5N, what is the magnitude of F2?
questions.explanation: The two forces are mutually perpendicular, so the resultant satisfies R squared = F1 squared + F2 squared. With R = 13 N and F1 = 5 N, F2 squared = 13 squared - 5 squared = 169 - 25 = 144. Hence F2 = 12 N. Therefore the missing force is 12.0 N, which corresponds to option 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A block-and-tackle system is used to lift a load of 20N through a vertical height of 10m. if the efficiency of the system is 40%, how much work is done against friction?
questions.explanation: Useful output work is the gain in gravitational potential energy of the load: 20 N x 10 m = 200 J. Efficiency equals useful output divided by input, so 0.40 = 200/input work. Hence input work = 500 J. The work done against friction is the wasted part: 500 - 200 = 300 J. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following devices are used to measure pressure? i. Aneroid barometer. ii. hydrometer. iii. hygrometer. iv. manometer.
questions.explanation: An aneroid barometer measures atmospheric pressure and a manometer measures gas or liquid pressure. A hydrometer measures relative density, while a hygrometer measures humidity. Therefore only items i and iv are pressure-measuring devices. Matching this set with the options gives option 3 as the correct answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A piece of wood of mass 40g and uniform cross-sectional area of 2cm2 floats upright in water. The length of the wood immersed is
questions.explanation: A floating body displaces its own weight of water, so the mass of displaced water equals the mass of the wood, 40 g. Since water has density 1 g per cubic centimetre, the displaced volume is 40 cubic centimetres. With cross-sectional area 2 square centimetres, immersed length = volume divided by area = 40/2 = 20 cm. Thus option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A column of air 10.0cm long is trapped in a tube at 27oC. What is the length of the volume at 100oC?
questions.explanation: At constant pressure, Charles's law applies: volume is proportional to absolute temperature. In a uniform tube, volume is proportional to length, so L1/T1 = L2/T2. Convert temperatures to kelvin: 27 degrees Celsius = 300 K and 100 degrees Celsius = 373 K. Thus L2 = 10.0 x 373/300 = 12.43 cm, which rounds to 12.4 cm. Option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A mass of gas at 7oC and 70cm of mercury has a volume of 1200cm3. Determine its volume at 27oC and pressure of 75cm of mercury.
questions.explanation: Use the combined gas law: P1V1/T1 = P2V2/T2. Convert temperatures to kelvin: 7 degrees Celsius = 280 K and 27 degrees Celsius = 300 K. Then V2 = 1200 x 70 x 300 divided by 75 x 280. Since 70/75 = 14/15 and 300/280 = 15/14, the factors cancel exactly, giving V2 = 1200 cubic centimetres. Option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An electric heater is used to melt a block of ice of mass 1.5kg. If the heater is powered by a 12V battery and a current of 20A flows through the coil, calculate the time taken to melt the block of ice at 0oC. [specific latent heat of fusion of ice = 336 x 103Jkg-1]
questions.explanation: Only latent heat is needed because the ice is already at 0 degrees Celsius. Required energy is Q = mL = 1.5 x 336 x 10^3 = 504000 J. The heater power is P = VI = 12 x 20 = 240 W. So time t = Q/P = 504000/240 = 2100 s = 35.0 minutes. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: From the kinetic theory of gases, temperature is a
options: form of energy and is proportional to the total kinetic energy of the molecules
form of energy and is proportional to the average kinetic energy of the molecules
physical property and is proportional to the total kinetic energy of the molecules
physical property and is proportional to the average kinetic energy of the molecules
questions.explanation: Temperature is not itself a form of energy. It is a physical property that indicates thermal state. From kinetic theory, the absolute temperature of a gas is proportional to the average kinetic energy per molecule, not the total kinetic energy of all molecules, because the total depends on the amount of gas present. Therefore option 3 is the correct statement.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A vibrator of frequency 60Hz is used in generating transverse stationary waves in a long thin wire, If the average distance between successive nodes on the wire is 45cm, find the speed of the transverse waves in the wire.
questions.explanation: In a stationary wave, the distance between successive nodes equals half a wavelength. Given node spacing 45 cm, we have lambda/2 = 0.45 m, so lambda = 0.90 m. Wave speed is v = f lambda = 60 x 0.90 = 54 m/s. Therefore the transverse wave speed is 54 m/s, which corresponds to option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When the tension in a sonometer wire is doubled, the ratio of the new frequency to the initial frequency is?
questions.explanation: For a stretched sonometer wire of fixed length and linear density, frequency varies directly as the square root of the tension. If the tension doubles, the new frequency becomes proportional to square root of 2T. Hence the ratio of new to original frequency is square root of 2T divided by square root of T, which is square root of 2. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In a sound wave in air, the adjacent rarefactions and compressions are separated by a distance of 17cm. If the velocity of the sound wave is 340ms-1. Determine the frequency
questions.explanation: In a longitudinal sound wave, a compression and the adjacent rarefaction are half a wavelength apart. So if their separation is 17 cm, then lambda/2 = 0.17 m and lambda = 0.34 m. Using v = f lambda with v = 340 m/s gives f = 340/0.34 = 1000 Hz. Hence option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Light of wavelength 5000 x 10-8cm travels in free space with a velocity of 3 x 108ms-1. What is its wavelength in glass of refractive index 1.5?
questions.explanation: When light enters glass, its frequency stays unchanged, but its speed and wavelength decrease. Refractive index satisfies n = wavelength in vacuum divided by wavelength in glass. Therefore wavelength in glass = 5000 x 10^-8 cm divided by 1.5 = 3333.3 x 10^-8 cm. To the given precision, this is 3333 x 10^-8 cm, so option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The plane mirrors in a kaleidoscope are usually placed
questions.explanation: A simple kaleidoscope commonly uses two plane mirrors inclined at 60 degrees. This arrangement gives repeated reflections that form the familiar symmetrical patterns. Parallel mirrors produce repeated images in a line, while perpendicular mirrors give a different image count and symmetry. Therefore the usual placement in a kaleidoscope is at an angle of 60 degrees, which is option 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A far sighted person cannot see objects that are less than 100cm away. If this person wants to read a book at 25cm, what type and focal length of lens does he need?
questions.explanation: A far-sighted person has a near point at 100 cm, so a reading lens must make a book at 25 cm appear as a virtual image at 100 cm. Using the thin lens formula with u = -25 cm and v = -100 cm gives 1/f = 1/25 - 1/100 = 3/100. Thus f about 33.3 cm, and the lens must be converging. Option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When a yellow card is observed through a blue glass, the card would appear.
questions.explanation: A yellow object reflects mainly red and green light and absorbs blue. A blue glass transmits blue light but absorbs most red and green light. Since the yellow card sends essentially no blue light through the filter, very little or no light reaches the eye. The card therefore appears black. Hence option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Dispersion of light by a glass prism is due to the
options: different speeds of the various colours in glass
questions.explanation: Dispersion by a prism occurs because different colours have different refractive indices in glass. Equivalently, they travel at different speeds in the glass and are refracted by different amounts. This separation produces the spectrum. The effect is not caused by glass defects, the glass having colours of its own, or density alone. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following pairs is NOT part of the electromagnetic spectrum? i. Radio waves. ii. Beta rays. iii. Gamma rays. iv. Alpha rays
questions.explanation: Radio waves and gamma rays are electromagnetic waves. Beta rays are streams of electrons or positrons, and alpha rays are helium nuclei, so both are particle radiations rather than members of the electromagnetic spectrum. Therefore the pair that is not part of the electromagnetic spectrum is ii and iv. This matches option 3, despite the duplicated wording in option 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Two insulated charged spheres of different sizes and carrying opposite charges are connected together by a metallic conductor. Current will flow from one sphere to the other until both sphere
options: carry the same magnitude and sign of charge
questions.explanation: When two charged conducting spheres are connected by a metallic conductor, charge flows because their electric potentials differ. The flow continues until electrostatic equilibrium is reached, and equilibrium requires equal potential, not equal charge or equal size. Spheres of different radii can end with different charges while still sharing the same potential. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When a number of identical small magnets are arranged in a line, the strength of the resultant magnet
options: ia largest when they are arranged end to end
is greatest when they are arrangedparallel with like poles adjacent to each other
depends only on the number of magnets provided they arev parallel
is greater when the magnets are arranged on a wooden surface than on a metaln surface
questions.explanation: Identical bar magnets give the strongest resultant when placed end to end with unlike poles touching, so their magnetic moments reinforce along the same line and form a longer effective magnet. Placing like poles adjacent in parallel is not the strongest arrangement, and the supporting surface material is irrelevant here. Therefore option 0 is the correct choice despite typographical errors in the text.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A bar magnet is most effectively demagnetized by
options: placing it in a N - S position and hitting it with a hammer
subjecting it to an electric current from a battery
bringing its north pole in contact with the north pole of a very strong magnet
questions.explanation: Heating a magnet strongly disturbs the alignment of its magnetic domains through thermal agitation, reducing or destroying its magnetization. Hammering can demagnetize in some cases, especially in the Earth's field, but it is less definitive than heating in the context of the given options. Therefore the most effective listed method is heating the magnet, which is option 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The resistance of a 5m uniform wire of cross-sectional area 0.2 x 10-6m2 is 0.425. What is the resistivity of the material of the wire?
questions.explanation: Resistivity is found from R = rho L/A, so rho = RA/L. With R = 0.425 ohm, A = 0.2 x 10^-6 square metres, and L = 5 m, rho = 0.425 x 0.2 x 10^-6 divided by 5 = 0.017 x 10^-6 = 1.7 x 10^-8 ohm metre. This matches option 3 exactly.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Three resistors, with substances 250\(\Omega\), 500\(\Omega\) and 1k\(\Omega\) are connected in series. A 6V battery is connected to either end of the combination. Calculate the pot3ential difference between the end of the 250\(\Omega\) resistor.
questions.explanation: In series, the same current flows through all three resistors. The total resistance is 250 + 500 + 1000 = 1750 ohms. Using Ohm’s law, the current is I = 6/1750 A, about 3.43 x 10^-3 A. The p.d. across the 250 ohm resistor is V = IR = (6/1750) x 250 = 0.857 V, which rounds to 0.86 V. That matches option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A calibrated potentiometer is used to measure the e.m.f. of a cell because the
options: internal resistance of a cell is small compared with that of the potentiometer
potentiometer takes no current from the cell
resistance of the potentiometer is less than that of a voltmeter
questions.explanation: A potentiometer measures e.m.f. by a null method. At balance, no current is drawn from the cell under test, so there is no voltage drop across its internal resistance. The measured value is therefore the true e.m.f. rather than a loaded terminal p.d. This is the essential reason for using a potentiometer, so option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The electrochemical equivalent of silver is 0.0012gC-1. If 36.0g of silver is to be deposited by electrolysis on a surface by passing a steady current for 5.0mins, the current must be
questions.explanation: For electrolysis, deposited mass is m = ZIt. Hence I = m/(Zt). Using m = 36.0 g, Z = 0.0012 g per coulomb, and t = 5.0 minutes = 300 s gives I = 36.0 divided by 0.0012 x 300 = 36.0/0.36 = 100 A. Therefore the required steady current is 100 A, which is option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When a radiation strikes a metal surface, electrons may be ejected from the metal. The maximum kinetic energy which may be acquired by an ejected electron depend on the
questions.explanation: In the photoelectric effect, the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons is given by Kmax = hf minus the work function. Since frequency and wavelength are inversely related, the maximum kinetic energy depends on the wavelength of the incident radiation. Intensity mainly changes the number of emitted electrons, not their maximum kinetic energy. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is TRUE of the particles emitted in radioactive disintegration?
options: the beta particle is the helium nucleus H
the alpha particle is lighter than the beta particle
the alpha particle is deflected more than the beta particle in a magnetic field
the beta particle is deflected more than the alpha particle in a magnetic field
questions.explanation: A beta particle is an electron or positron, while an alpha particle is a helium nucleus. In a magnetic field, deflection depends on charge-to-mass ratio. Because beta particles have much smaller mass, their charge-to-mass ratio is far larger than that of alpha particles, so they bend more strongly. Therefore the true statement is that the beta particle is deflected more than the alpha particle.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Eight alpha decays and six beta decays are necessary before an atom of 2 \(^{238}_{92}U\) achieves stability. The final product in the chain has an atomic number of
questions.explanation: Each alpha decay lowers the atomic number by 2, while each beta minus decay raises it by 1. Starting from uranium with atomic number 92, eight alpha decays reduce it by 16 to 76. Six beta decays then increase it by 6 to 82. So the final stable product has atomic number 82, which is option 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following are the correct SI units of the quantities indicated? i.N(Force) II. N/m (Torque) iii. watt(Power) iv. kgms-2(Momentum)
questions.explanation: Force has SI unit newton, so item i is correct. Torque should have unit newton metre, not newton per metre, so item ii is wrong. Power is measured in watt, so item iii is correct. Momentum should be kilogram metre per second, not kilogram metre per second squared, so item iv is wrong. Therefore only i and iii are correct, giving option 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A lorry travels 10km northwards, 4km eastwards, 6km southwards, 4km westwards to arrive at a point T. What is the total displacement?
questions.explanation: Treat each part of the journey as a displacement vector. The 4 km eastward motion and the 4 km westward motion cancel completely, leaving no net east-west displacement. Vertically, 10 km north minus 6 km south leaves 4 km north. The attached diagram is consistent with this vector cancellation. Therefore the total displacement is 4 km north, option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Two forces whose resultant is 100N, are at right angle to each other. If one of them makes an angle 30o with the resultant, determine its magnitude.
questions.explanation: The two perpendicular forces and their resultant form a right triangle. If one force makes 30 degrees with the resultant, that force is adjacent to the 30 degree angle, while the resultant is the hypotenuse. Hence its magnitude is F = R cos 30 degrees = 100 x 0.866 = 86.6 N. Therefore option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following quantities are scalars? i. Electrical potential ii. Torque iii. Momentum iv. Kinetic energy
questions.explanation: Electrical potential is a scalar quantity because it has magnitude only. Torque has direction and is treated as a vector, and momentum is also a vector since it depends on direction of motion. Kinetic energy is scalar. Therefore the scalar quantities listed are i and iv only, which corresponds to option 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When taking a penalty kick, a footballer applies a force of 30.0N for a period of 0.05s. if the mass of the ball is 0.075kg, calculate the speed with which the ball moves off.
questions.explanation: Impulse equals change in momentum. The ball starts from rest, so Ft = mv. Using F = 30.0 N and t = 0.05 s gives impulse 30.0 x 0.05 = 1.5 N s. Therefore v = 1.5/0.075 = 20.0 m/s. The speed with which the ball moves off is 20.00 m/s, so option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A particle starts from rest and moves with a constant acceleration of 0.5ms\(^{-2}\). The distance covered by the particle in 10s is?
questions.explanation: The particle starts from rest, so initial velocity u = 0. For constant acceleration, distance is s = ut + 1/2 at squared. Substituting a = 0.5 m/s squared and t = 10 s gives s = 0 + 1/2 x 0.5 x 10 squared = 0.25 x 100 = 25 m. Thus the distance covered is 25.0 m, which is option 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A 20-toothed gear wheel drives a 60-toothed one. If the angular speed of the smaller wheel is 120 rev s-1, the angular speed of the larger wheel is
questions.explanation: For meshing gears, the angular speed is inversely proportional to the number of teeth because the tangential speeds at contact are equal. Thus N1 omega1 = N2 omega2. With 20 teeth and 120 rev/s for the smaller gear, and 60 teeth for the larger gear, omega2 = 20 x 120 divided by 60 = 40 rev/s. Therefore option 1 is correct, not the supplied answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A force, 10N, drags a mass 10kg on a horizontal table with an acceleration of 0.2ms. If the acceleration due to gravity is 10ms-1, the coefficient of friction between the moving mass and the table is
questions.explanation: The net horizontal force is applied force minus friction. So 10 - friction = ma = 10 x 0.2 = 2 N, giving friction = 8 N. On a horizontal table, the normal reaction is mg = 10 x 10 = 100 N. Therefore the coefficient of friction is mu = 8/100 = 0.08. Option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A body whose mass is 2kg and has a volume of 500cm3 just floats when completely immersed in a liquid. Calculate the density of the liquid
questions.explanation: If the body just floats when completely immersed, its density equals the density of the liquid. The body's density is mass divided by volume. Convert 500 cubic centimetres to 5 x 10^-4 cubic metres. Then density = 2 divided by 5 x 10^-4 = 4.0 x 10^3 kg/m^3. Therefore the liquid density is 4.0 x 10^3 kg/m^3, which is option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The product PV where P is pressure and V is volume has the same unit as
questions.explanation: Pressure has unit pascal, which is newton per square metre, and volume has unit cubic metre. Multiplying gives newton metre. A newton metre is a joule, the unit of work or energy. Force alone is measured in newtons, power in joules per second, and acceleration in metres per second squared. Therefore PV has the same unit as energy.
